So you wanna know how this compares to other farming sims, eh? Lemme tell ya what I've noticed so far as someone who loves this genre maybe a liiiitttllleeeee too much.

TLDR/OVERALL: A solid 9.5/10 for me so far. Probably one of the most polished games I've played with an incredible amount of QoL that really raises the bar on what other farming sims should have. Gives a fresh feel to a lot of mechanics while also feeling cozy and charming.

---
THE GOOD:
---

All cutscenes are voice acted, and as someone who usually switches to Japanese immediately because the English sounds so abysmal, this one is full of life without sounding stilted and forced. Characters sound so realistic and earnest, and it's a joy to let each line fully play out which is rare for me.

You can jump and water crops. You can jump and harvest. You can jump and plant seeds! Everything feels so smooth to do, and it removes a ton of the monotony that these games can foist on you. It feels very refreshing to farm again because you can bulk do almost anything.

You get handed a nice house, and no, your grandpa didn't die and leave it to you and your first quest is to fix some broken floorboards. This game treats you like someone who knows what a farming sim is, while allowing you to play with your hand held if you choose. It's so nice to just get tools out the gate with a quick explanation in a "We know you know, go for it!" style.

If you like other SoS games, you'll also find some familiar faces from other titles! But everyone feels so much more fleshed out in this one. Everybody actually feels like their own person, instead of a slapstick trope like a lot of farming sims seem to be falling into these days.

THE BAZAAR. Okay, I am in love. Getting to sell my stuff at a little booth is just amazing. You have a morning shift, a break to shop, and an afternoon shift on Saturdays. Yes you can sell things in between the week still, so you're not stuck. But oh my gosh are the mechanics just so fun. People look for a certain item? Great, swap it out at your table! Click on people to sell stuff, ring your bell while hollering at your PC screen "BUY MY TURNIPS AND BUGS!" It's honestly so fun.

You can change your look AT ANY TIME FOR FREE from the vanity in your room. As a chronic aesthetic changer, this is a GODSEND.

Also there's just so many QoL things I can't even remember them all to mention here. Getting to wave at people instead of needing to click on each one to raise social, having a little notification pop up to tell you when you can view a cutscene somewhere in town instead of wandering aimlessly, etc. There's so many things in the few hours I've played that made me go "Why don't more games do this?!"

---
THE MEH:
---

I find a lot of NPC outfits sorta doofy, but that's personal taste and I know it's just the SoS style. I also don't love that a lot of characters seem to look so young all the time, but that's honestly such a tiny thing haha.

Also the days are REALLY fast. I mean really fast. I feel like I blink and it's over, but I've also been playing a lot of Fields of Mistria and Sun Haven lately, so take that with a grain of salt.

The only two GOOD female hairstyles are locked behind the DLC. There's maybe 4 feminine hairs vs 10+ masculine crop cuts that all look vaguely similar. This kinda sucks, but eh, what can ya do?

---
THE BAD:
---

I can't even call this bad because it's really not THAT bad, aha. But fishing just takes a long time with how fast the day goes. It takes like 2 in game hours to catch a thing, since it's about a minute of game time per real life second, so it doesn't feel very worth it.

Before you correct me or interject; Yes, I know this game predates Animal Crossing, Stardew, and Minecraft, and most other farming/life sims.  I mention those games because I am constantly comparing each new install to them (and the new games never stack up).  I opted to give this series a try and OH. MY. GOD.  This is it.  The gameplay loop, the graphics, the voice acting (while not completely voice acted, there's still enough), and the organic nature in which things occur.  

High level: Grow crops, gather materials, catch fish/bugs, then craft and sell them at the weekly Bazaar.  You goal is to re-establish this little market each Saturday, and every Sunday morning (in game) I find myself game-planning for the next Bazaar.  

If you are looking to satiate that Stardew/Animal Crossing itch, this is the game.  I cannot recommend it enough, and I hope you enjoy it as much as I am.

I’m a HUGE Harvest Moon fan. I’ve played all the original HM titles, every Story of Seasons remake, plus games like Stardew Valley and Fields of Mistria. Since the SoS remakes started, I’ve had pretty mixed feelings. Friends of Mineral Town and A Wonderful Life were fun for the nostalgia hit, but they didn’t add much beyond that. Pioneers of Olive Town tried to push forward, but it felt messy and overloaded, like Marvelous was chasing expectations instead of making something with intention.

Grand Bazaar feels different. It feels right. This game takes the heart and soul of what makes a Harvest Moon or Story of Seasons game special, learns from the issues of PoOT, and creates something truly beautiful. The VOICE ACTING adds so much personality, there are tons of QoL improvements (storage and inventory management especially is miles better), and the new mechanics feel purposeful and fun instead of just “because other farm sims have it.” The fishing is actually enjoyable, the gameplay loop is incredibly addictive, and the bazaar system is brilliant.

I never played the original Grand Bazaar, so there’s zero nostalgia bias here. This is just flat-out the best SoS game I’ve played so far. The romance events are super charming (though I’m still crossing my fingers for rival marriages to return someday), and after only a few hours I can already tell I’m going to sink a ton of time into this.

If you’ve been waiting for a Story of Seasons game that feels both true to its roots and fresh in the right ways, this is it. Please support it. And Marvelous, if you’re listening, Animal Parade or Tree of Tranquility remakes when?!

I played the original Harvest Moon: Grand Bazaar game a lot as a kid, and this is an incredibly faithful remake of the original! I'm so glad that they added QOL improvements into the game for the farming portions so you have more time in the game day to check windmills, care for the animals, and run around the wilderness to find ores and materials. The Bazaar mini-game was also improved, and I like how hectic it can get! Still one of the most fun parts by far. 

Probably the best QOL they added in the whole game was that they made it so you can see when Heart Events are occuring on the map. It's SO much easier to go and catch the events so you can progress your relationships with characters. No more do you need to have a wiki on hand to jot down all the events!
Although, surprisingly enough, I feel like the friendship gain with characters is REALLY fast in this game compared to the original, but it's been a long time since I played the old one, so it's very likely I just wasn't doing the friendship quests as a kid lol. You also can romance any of the bachelors and bachelorettes in this game which is pretty cool, mostly because I never got to know any of the other girl characters very well in my original game playthrough, so it's fun to see both sides!

It also goes without saying that the graphics are totally adorable! It really feels like they took the old game and gave it a modern shine with a handful of improvements! It still has the classic feel of the original gameplay loop and I'm all here for it!

Best story of seasons as of year 2025. This is a grand remake of a 3ds game. If you are familiar with the formula, you will surely enjoy this game. Don't expect caves and combat on this game as this is purely a foraging/fishing/farming game with npc romance mechanic. For starters, the bazaar and the trend system is the core mechanic of this game which has very high replayabillity due to the persistent ranking system (From town bazaar to World rank bazaar) that also unlocks certain upgradeable items or system on the game. Crafting and Cooking also has a lot of varieties and items that you can create with specific positive buffs which will be useful on your post-game sessions.

It offers a very rewarding feeling as you progress and reaches the World Rank Bazaar that unlocks everything to make your farming life easier and cozier. Hopefully, they add more things here with the future updates like more NPC dialogues and events.

I've enjoyed this franchise for over a decade, and in my opinion, this is the best one since SoS:ToT by far. I was hesitant to pick this one up because the last few titles felt like attempts to bankroll on Harvest Moon nostalgia that failed to be transformative enough to enjoy on modern systems, but Grand Bazaar breathed the soul back into the Seasons games that was lost during the transition to Switch.

 Making money is fun again, and voice acting is great. The characters don't feel like slightly tweaked imitations of one another, and for the first time in a hot minute, I haven't been able to single out my favorites, because they're all great. Exploring and movement is fresh and dynamic, making this feel like the least "rigid" gameplay in a sense. I could sing praises about this game all day long, and would recommend it to anyone - particularly if you liked Rune Factory 4 or Trio of Towns.

[h2] A faithful remake with tons of new content that is certain to satisfy new and veteran players [/h2]

Harvest Moon: Grand Bazaar for the DS was already a fantastic game and the bazaar was a beloved feature that set the game apart from the others. The windmill system allowed players to craft a wider variety of products to offer at their bazaar stand.

Fast-forward to 2025, and Story of Seasons: Grand Bazaar keeps all of the special elements intact while adding lots of depth and new systems that will keep players entertained for a long time. 

To name a few:
-You can now decorate your bazaar stand to gain buffs
-Use the Sprites you meet in game to help sell items faster (happiness minigame)
-New currency to exchange with the Sprites
-Sprites can improve the quality of items by submitting items from that category
-Individualized character requests
-Food buffs
-New bazaar stalls
-Fully voiced special scenes (voice acting is overall very good as well)

...and much more. I haven't even unlocked everything possible at the time of this review. The only complaint I have is that some of the character names changed but that's a small thing. This truly is the best remake of a Harvest Moon game so far. If they use this formula for their next planned remakes, they're sure to be successful.

Game has a lot going for it with a lot to do.  The Bazaar is much fun because you are always trying to make as much money as possible every Saturday.  The game overall is just challenging overall, without being super baby hand-holding like many of the cozy games that are released these days. 

This game is not on the same level as StarDew Valley, or even Coral Island, but it definitely created its own niche in the cozy game marketplace.  I am enjoying the game myself, my only issue with it is that its stylized too much like a typical mobile game, especially in the graphics and UI department, which is not something I usually go for, but I can overlook it because I like the game overall.

The bazaar is such a fun twist on the farming sim genre. It's cute and cozy. Though the farming plot is pretty small, the days go by fast enough that more space to farm might be too much to start. The days go by 1 minute every second. You have to go to sleep by 9 PM to wake up at 6 AM and will wake up later and later the next day the longer you stay up. The characters have some pretty good personality though you can get some repeat lines with a few of them pretty easily. I like that the trending items (which sell for more) stay the same the entire season so you can save up your items and its not a constant change. One of my biggest cons of the game so far is that there is no mines. Instead you mine ore that appears in the mountains and town roughly twice per day. And that ore does not always give you what it looks like. If you mine silver ore, you might get iron instead. Same for copper. It's a little frustrating but again the in game time moves so fast that I guess an actual mine probably wouldn't work. the barn animals mechanics are a little confusing but overall, its a bit of a refreshing difference from the previous story of seasons that draws out the enjoyment and always makes sure you have something to do! (especially if you want to make friends with anyone!)

The original Harvest Moon Grand Bazaar (HMGB) was my favorite game of all time as a kid and the very reason why I fell in love with the farming simulation genre. It was the first farming game that centered its core game-play loop over selling your crops/harvests at a weekend bazaar, and while it was challenging planning days in advance to make a killing at the bazaar, it was also equal parts rewarding. The premise of the game was deceptively simple, and each time you thought the game had shown you everything it had to offer, it presented you with new mechanics that pushed the breadth of the game even further. 

For the past 17 years, none of the games I've played could ever come close to scratching this unique itch that HMGB gave, that is until this Story of Seasons remake. This remake takes whatever HMGB had to offer and dials it up to 11. There is so much heart in this remake - the graphics are gorgeous, the voice acting breathes so much life into the characters, the portraits are beautifully nostalgic, and the game-play is as addictive as ever - everything feels fresh yet familiar at the same time. In this modern age where the farming sim genre is plagued with low-effort, half-baked out of Early Access cash grabs, SoSGB reminds me why I fell in love with the genre in the first place, and proves how the developers of HMGB were completely ahead of their time for designing a variety of mechanics that remain fresh and unique 17 years later. 

Thank you so much to all the wonderful developers at Marvelous for giving HMGB/SoSGB all the attention and love it deserves, I can't emphasise how much it means to me to be able to see Grand Bazaar come alive again in 2025. The future of Story of Seasons has never looked brighter, and I can't wait to see how the remakes of other games in the Harvest Moon franchise will turn out!

I’ve been into farming sims for a while. Played the first Story of Seasons on 3DS over 10 years ago and loved it. Tried Trio of Towns but dropped it after a few hours. Then came Stardew Valley, which I sunk 300+ hours into — still the best farming sim imo thanks to to mods. Since then, nothing really scratched the itch

A friend with 20+ hours in Grand Bazaar told me to give it a shot. I’m 13 hours in, it’s been great so far.

Gameplay (9/10)
The bazaar system is the big hook. Instead of shipping crops, you prep for a weekly market. It adds planning and strategy — what to grow, what to craft, what to sell. It makes every week feel more purposeful, and it’s more fun than I expected.

Story (7/10)
Not a huge deal for me, but the characters are fine. Designs are solid, enough to keep the town lively, though nothing too deep.

Music (8/10)
Cozy background tunes, fits the mood. I usually swap it out for my own playlist (Doom music + farming = weirdly satisfying).

Graphics (9/10)
Colorful and charming. The oversized cow models looked strange at first, but I’ve gotten used to them. Overall, the style fits the cozy vibe really well.

World (9/10)

Okay, so to start out I am a BIG fan of this game, and I've played a ton of HM/SOS games in my time. I loved it on it's original release and I'll be comparing it to that as well as giving an independent review.

To summarize a lot of questions /I/ had when seeing it was getting a remaster, It is very SIMILAR to it's original DS release. Same vibe, same missions, same cozy feel that older SOS games had. There are still a few differences that I'd like to have seen.
-You can no longer jump into the water to prospect for trash or treasure at the bottom of rivers. 
    I really liked this feature (though it did use a lot of stamina) as it was a really unique feature I has seen in no other game of this type. Usually the water was just a void or impossible to enter .

- Nature Sprites have more purpose 
- There are Quests now for the villagers which I don't recall being in the DS version, and this breaks up the day to day tasks so it doesn't just hum together (a sad fault with any farming sim) 

-There are new characters to interact with and they all seem pretty fleshed out (Random NPC who?)
-And we can't forget the voice acting, which was a HUGE thing to add into this game but...also leads to a small complaint that it's only in English. 
     (Nothing against the voice acting, but the English VA cue is pretty small so some voices just sound bleh)


Now after playing it for 13 hours, I can give it a solid run down,

PROs
---------------------------------------

-There's plenty to do and harvest(though give your low qual stuff to the sprites to boost quality)
-The game actually informs you(roughly) of what villagers like, making presents easier
-Felix gives me Armstrong Vibes and I'm down for it
- Because of some new mechanics and questmaking, I can always check what I need before I need it (have yet to be proved wrong until I said this)
-MC customization is wide spread and not gender-locked (can be changed anytime)

-Content is STILL BEING ADDED! 
    Usually in these types of games, once it's released that's it, but this game just got an update a few days ago




Cons
-----------------------------------------

-Voice Acting is limited to English (or maybe region locked?)
- There's still small glitches where I recommend saving often in your house, as it will bug out to your last auto save (beware of jumping near fences, you WILL get stuck if there's a barrier )
-Some of the progression seems a little slow, and some of it way too fast to be a challenge (one of the sprites takes forageables, including low qual Grass and rocks, so they can progress waaaaaay faster than other sprites while some, like the one for Honey/Products, you can't even touch yet)




All in all it comes down to the important question,

"Is it worth it?"

Yes the game is one of the more expensive SOS titles, with DLC and Deluxe versions raising the price anymore, but it's not just the same game printed with a new title, Voice acting, and new artstyles. 

It used the DS version as a base and expanded it to compete with even their own titles, and so far, though I am still new in the game, I can not say I regret the purchase. 

It's a cozy game after a long day of work, with a very relaxing soundtrack (rainy days best yo) and it's great that one of my top 3 titles got a remaster. I love the story based games of HM and SOS, as they feel more "full" of content. 

I would say worth it, personally.

[h1]A charming revisit to a beloved classic -- [i]STORY OF SEASONS: Grand Bazaar[/i] is a slow burn full of charisma.[/h1]

While I still have so much of the game left to play, I already love it and I want to review it. If you ever played the original [i]Harvest Moon[/i] title, you will really enjoy this one. It is pretty faithful, and all the new additions serve to make it even more enjoyable. From quality of life changes to some new, welcome additions to the cast, the game is completely recognizable but with a much appreciated fresh coat of paint. Coming back to Zephyr Town feels like coming back to a familiar place, which makes me excited to play this during Autumn as it goes without saying that, as one would expect from [i]STORY OF SEASONS[/i], cozy vibes abound. 

The voice acting takes some getting used to, but it isn't unwelcome. It's very interesting for a change, actually. I think every voice actor delivered strongly. This game also heralds in the triumphant return of portraits, which add so much whimsy and personality to not only the game but every character. The new marriage candidates also add some diversity to the lineup, and I really think they are well-written characters, especially Diana. The whole setting feels alive, the bazaar is fun and gives you something to look forward to every week, and I really love the animals in this rendition. I would say, in my opinion, the animals feel the liveliest in this game than any other predecessor. Letting them out, watching them roam and play, there seems to have been a lot of detail put into the livestock this time around. 

Visually this game is very pretty and it's a joy to move around it, especially because of the glider mechanic. I love the fishing mechanic in this game, it isn't overly complex like some farming games. It isn't super easy either. There is a good amount of character customization, including pronouns which was surprising. The only thing about character customization that I wish would change moving forward is the character size. I wish there was an option to be a taller male, since with the character we are given by default, you are basically the shortest guy in the town and also look very young. Even though I understand the reason, giving you a blank canvas that will work for male or female players, I wish you could change the body shapes and styles eventually in a [i]STORY OF SEASONS[/i] title. The events also are pretty lively and also frequent, although some like the honey festival don't have a specific start or end and don't have a scene or anything particularly special about them. 

A lot of games in the "cozy genre" are very lazily made or rest on their laurels, knowing the expectations of their audience are usually low. This game isn't lazy and has a lot of love and care put into it. 

TL;DR: This game is so cute and fun. It will be perfect for Autumn.

[h1]Story of Seasons: Grand Bazaar – A Refined Throwback[/h1]

[i]A remake of Harvest Moon: Grand Bazaar, now in 3D with voiced NPCs, bringing back the cozy farm-life mechanics with some smart refinements.[/i]

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Farming & Production[/h2]
The familiar mechanics are all here:
[list]
[*]Crops that can grow across multiple seasons
[*]Honey making and mushroom growing
[*]Classic barn animals with the usual care routines
[*]etc...
[/list]

What stands out are the [b]production chains[/b] via the windmills. These mechanics existed in older titles, but here they feel more polished and satisfying. In this entry, combining items boost overall item value while saving inventory slots in your bazaar inventory, making it possible for you to gain more profits. 

Compared to [i]Pioneers of Olive Town[/i], where you need various makers across your farm, this game condenses production into just [b]three windmills[/b], each with its own specialty. This makes things tidier, though progression eventually feels bottlenecked by their limited capacity. Buffs / modifications exist for the windmills, but they unlock fairly late.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]The Bazaar[/h2]
Instead of dumping items into a shipping bin daily, you [b]stockpile during the week[/b] and sell everything at the bazaar every Saturday in two time slots.

This system makes selling far more engaging:
[list]
[*]You can earn more profit than selling directly to stores
[*]Merchants offer unique items and upgrades only during bazaar days
[*]It adds a fun “competition” feel as you push for better sales each week
[/list]

The bazaar is the defining feature here, and for me it’s a clever twist on the series’ formula.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Pain Points[/h2]
Not everything is sunshine and turnips, though. A few issues stood out:

[list]
[*][b]Storage limits[/b] – Your bag and warehouse fill up very quickly, and there’s no way to build extra storage. Early game becomes a grind for warehouse upgrades.
[*][b]Mining (or lack thereof)[/b] – No dedicated mine exists. Ores and gems are random drops from scattered stones, making tool upgrades tedious. You can buy ores at the bazaar, but they’re stuck at 0.5 quality.
[*][b]Rotting mechanic[/b] – Produce spoils over time. It’s only mildly frustrating, especially when trying to cook using produces from previous seasons, because food can give you strong buffs. However, there are usually alternative recipes giving the same buffs that you can unlock.
[/list]

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Verdict[/h2]
Despite its flaws, [b]Story of Seasons: Grand Bazaar[/b] is a charming and enjoyable addition to the series. The bazaar mechanic feels fresh, production is streamlined, and the farming loop is as addictive as ever.

[b]Highly recommended for both veterans and newcomers to the series.[/b]

It's been a long time since I've latched onto a farming sim game like this! The gameplay loop is so addictive, but what I really connected with is the overall style of the game and its perfect suspension of realism.

I played the original DS games when I was younger, but was never a big fan of the 3D art style the Story of Seasons games adopted from that point on. With this Grand Bazaar remake, I feel as though its art style finally captures a lot of the charm I was missing from previous titles. (Not the least because of the return of illustrated character portraits as a dialogue accent!) 

As for the "realism" in the game — the wind mechanic is such a game changer, and so is making crops perishable. These add great stakes to each in-game week and I found a natural rhythm with them after a while of playing. Love the animals in this game as well; the multiple interactions possible each day and the focus on not only livestock but also pets as helpers on the farm made being in the game so much more appealing to me. These elements are realistic, but not so much that it burdens gameplay.

I do think the story is a little weaker than I would like, and the character dynamics might lean towards being a little too simple, but it really helpsme progress through the game to have friendship progression locked after milestones. That may not be to everyone's taste, but it helps me explore the rest of the game without being too focused on relationships.

The cutscene I absolutely had to review is the one where Clara gets ambushed by Kevin’s mischievous bug party. It’s rare for me to praise English voice acting, but in this case, it’s really well done! Some characters even sound better than the Japanese voices. With all due respect, I started playing with English voices first, then switched to Japanese, but I felt that characters we meet early on, like Mayor Felix, fit the English performance perfectly. And honestly, I couldn’t handle the cutscene where Gabriel, starving and desperate, goes to Derek.

If there's a Story of Seasons game anyone should play, this is probably it. They could've probably done a little bit better on the art front because your character looks so incredibly lame if you go for "Type 1" body type, theoretically the "male-er" body type, though both body types look and act very feminine. You get over it very quickly though, but when you see other male characters in the game it feels very sad because I'd rather play as one of those guys than this dude(?) basis looks.

That aside, this is the most fun gameplay loop I have had in any Story of Seasons/HM game. The pacing is perfect because you define it, it is a milestone based pacing which is crazy because I was already at Gold tools in the first season of the game, which would be impossible in most other SoS games. They got rid of all the bloat from most games and they made movement and farming very convenient, and also put the tool upgrades in your own hands bypassing the whole "give your tool to the blacksmith" trope. Same with a lot of other things.

I think having a milestone based pacing is a game changer because now I don't have anxiety about "oh what if I miss doing this on this season, then the only way I can do it is next year" which used to be so annoying. Nor does it make you wait seasons for something to happen, you always have a mini-goal of sorts all the time that you have to move towards so you remain engrossed in the game.

Additionally there's so much storage in this game and it is really not hard to get more, making it so easy to just hoard stuff and not have to feel like you are running out. And I probably haven't even scratched the surface on the amount of content left still. Best Story of Seasons I have played so far, though tbf I haven't played many (I have only played from To2T/3T, FoMT, AWL, Innocent Life, Hero of Leaf Valley, etc.), so take it as you will.

I haven't finished it yet but I can already tell this is one of the better entries in the SOS series. This is the best SOS has ever looked - the portraits are as classic and charming as ever and the 3D models are so detailed and expressive. The voice acting is great - it's not something I was expecting them to ever do, or something I was expecting to like either so I was pleasantly surprised twice there because I think it really elevates the experience in this game and gives the characters and cutscenes a lot of life.

The game is a little overbearing and handholdy at the start, and bazaar gameplay isn't as snappy as I remember it being in the original, which I did play many years ago. I think this is basically my only criticism so far. I can see the storage being one box for EVERYTHING being a problem for some people, who may be in more organised habits from other farming sim games that allow you to have multiple areas of storage for different things, but this doesn't bother me personally and if it doesn't bother you either then I don't think there's anything not to love about this game.

The game is very unique in that the cashflow part of farm management is frontloaded during bazaar days. The bazaar mechanic is very fun and very unique and something that had made the original (and this version!) stand out among farming simulators. I also love the setting and its concept as a breezy town. The NPCs are lively and likeable. The wind riding mechanic and windmill mechanics really draw attention to the Zephyr Town's breezes and it makes for a very fun, engaging and convincing concept for a setting. The glider takes a bit of getting used to - don't be like me and try to use it like Zelda's paraglider. There's not so much control - you're at the mercy of the wind so pay attention to the direction and strength it's blowing in! Since it doesn't take you very far on non-windy days and basically blows in one direction, it's clearly not meant to be considered a main transport method. It's just a little easier to get home from the mountains, or to the bazaar from home sometimes.

All in all, really enjoying it so far 20hrs in and imagine I have quite a bit of the game left to go at this standard - which is exciting, to say the least.

This game is an actual update and remake, unlike FOMT and AWL (don't get me wrong, I loved those games, but I wish we got more). I'm glad to see Marvelous is upping their game once again. They're the grandfather of farming sims and it would be a shame if they couldn't keep up with new titles and developers. People are saying this is the best SOS game yet, though I think I need more time to see if it's as complete a game as Animal Parade -- IMO best in the series -- and also I still think AWL beats it in terms of pure vibes (and cow design).

What I liked:
- Gameplay loop is addictive and always leaves you wanting more. 

- Upgrades are frontloaded to get you into the loop faster.

- The bazaar being only once a week makes it feel like the stakes are higher compared to shipping goods daily. If you don't manage your production well then you'll only see your money next week.

- Time passes faster than many recent farm sims, which means you actually have to manage your time. No more completing all your farm chores, fishing, socialising, and foraging before 12pm. This can be a con, depending on how you like to play these games.

- Characters were refreshed but kept the core of their old designs, unlike Mineral Town. The new characters are also very well-integrated into the story... unlike Mineral Town. 

- Graphics and art direction are some of the best in the series.


What I disliked:
- Marvelous has had close to 30 years to make these games and they still came up with this inventory system. The number of items you amass can and will get overwhelming, but you get two little poots of storage space. This may have been intentional but I HATE it. 

- Inventory quick menu feels a little clunky.

- Controls are a little slippery at times. 

- I know people love the bubble cows but pleaeeeease bring back the AWL cows and not these monstrosities.

Honestly, the best title in a long while.

I always loved the original DS version, but this one took that version and built upon it rather than changed it completely. They're still the same characters we know and love, but written to be a lot less flat. Time does go by fast in this game, but so did the original DS games. There's no features that were sacrificed for the sake of any superficial interactivity such as online sharing or turning the farm into a gallery. If this is the direction the Story of Seasons franchise will be going, then I will be looking forward to the next one, especially if its an original title that follows the direction that its going.

[h1][b]STORY OF SEASONS: Grand Bazaar? Wind, Markets, and Cozy Grind—Finally Back in Form![/b][/h1]

"A slow-burn farm life that blossoms: windmills and glider joy, a weekly bazaar loop that eats hours, vivid voices and portraits, plus tons of smart QoL—held back a bit by early pacing and hit-or-miss tunes."

[h1][b][1] Intro : [/b][/h1]

Once a DS favorite, Grand Bazaar returns as more than a coat of paint. Players call it the best the series has felt in years—bigger world, new characters, voiced cutscenes, and a reworked loop that makes Saturdays (Bazaar Day) the star. Several reviewers hit 50–60 hours without noticing the clock, praising how welcoming it is for newcomers while staying deep for veterans with trends, freshness, and stall strategy.

[h1][b][2] Game Experience : [/b][/h1]

Your week is a cozy cadence: tend fields and animals, craft with windmills, prep displays, then ring the bell and sell, sell, sell. The bazaar is lively—customize your stall, chase trends, and feel that hit of satisfaction when you sell out. Between markets, Zephyr Town feels alive: portraits give everyone personality, voiced story scenes pull you in, and there’s simply more dialogue than before—many note returning cameos and a couple of brand-new candidates that spice up courting.

Movement and chores are snappier. You jump over gaps, ride the wind on a glider, and even just waving to neighbors counts—no more stopping to chat with every single villager. The map shows where folks are, storage is reachable from multiple spots, bulk crafting is a breeze, sorting takes one button, and the trophy shelf turns achievements into cozy décor. Harvest Sprites now pitch in with their own little systems, and animals feel livelier—letting them out to roam is a joy. Fishing hits a sweet spot: not too fussy, not too simple.

Presentation gets a chorus of thumbs-up. Reviewers gush over petals drifting as you walk, swaying grass, a town clock that shows in-game time, and the overall “prettiest SoS yet.” Voice acting “takes a minute to adjust” for some, but many end up loving how it elevates events and distinct personalities. Performance? Smooth and polished for most players.

Not everything lands. A few wish for more fresh activities midweek while waiting for Saturday. The soundtrack divides: some tracks delight while others grate, with a couple of veterans preferring the DS-era vibe. Early hours can feel slow. A festival or two (like the honey event) lacks special scenes. Character customization gets praise for pronouns and open romance, but one reviewer wants body-type/height options—your farmer can look a bit too short and youthful. Still, the overall feeling is “this one’s made with love,” not a lazy remake. Bonus: a tiny Pinefly DLC supports real-world conservation and gives a cute outfit + glider.

[h2][b][3] Pros and Cons : [/b][/h2]

[b](+) The Good Stuff / What Rocked / Why You'll Love It:[/b]
[list]
[*]Weekly bazaar loop is addictive; trends/freshness make sales feel strategic and fun.
[*]Windmills for crafting, jumping, and glider travel keep chores brisk and exploration playful.
[*]Gorgeous visuals, expressive portraits, and full voice scenes make Zephyr Town feel alive.
[*]Big QoL sweep: map NPC tracker, bulk crafting, easy sorting, multi-point storage, wave-to-greet.
[*]New characters, cameos, Harvest Sprites systems, lively animals, and achievement display shelf.
[*]Inclusive options (pronouns, romance flexibility) and overall polished performance.
[/list]

[b](-) The Bad Stuff / What Sucked / Why You Might Rage:[/b]
[list]
[*]Early game runs slow; some players want more midweek variety between bazaars.
[*]Music quality swings from lovely to grating; a few prefer the classic OST.
[*]A couple of festivals feel light on bespoke scenes or structure.
[*]Character creator lacks body-type/height options; farmer can look overly short/young.
[*]If you want heavy challenge or complex sim layers, the cozy loop may feel too gentle.
[/list]

[h2][b][4] Final Thoughts / The Verdict : [/b][/h2]

Grand Bazaar isn’t just “not dookie”—it’s a heartfelt return to what fans fell for: a warming routine, a town that breathes, and bazaar Saturdays that genuinely matter. For new players, it’s an easy recommendation; for veterans burned by recent entries, it feels like redemption. Expect a comfy slow-burn with modern polish and a few rough notes in the soundtrack and early pacing. Verdict: Cozy classic reborn — 9/10 for series fans and chill farmers; 8/10 if you crave denser midweek gameplay or a bolder score.

An amazing remake of a nostalgic favorite of the Harvest Moon franchise. This game is eating up all my free time. I can't seem to put it down. Gardening and ranching do not take up your entire day or use up all your stamina (once you've upgraded your tools a little bit), so there's a good balance of time and energy to dedicate to other activities and bonding with the townspeople.

The bazaar stall is so fun to run. It makes me wish running your own shop/stall was a mechanic in more HM/SoS games. Crafting in this game isn't overly complicated, which is an issue I've had with some recent SoS titles that leaned more in the Stardew Valley direction (devs please don't ever do that again). Being able to have pets and train them to help with moving livestock is a feature that exists in a lot of HM/SoS games, but I think this game does it the best of all the titles I've played so far. The freedom to have multiple pets of each type of different breeds and mixes is a nice touch. It makes it so I don't feel like I'm missing out on multiple breed options I like. The cute little training minigame also makes petting and training them feel less like a boring chore, and more like bonding with an actual pet.

STORY OF SEASONS: Grand Bazaar is not just another re-skin of the older game with barely any changes made (cough cough SoS AWL). It’s a full on, ground up remake that removed most of what held the original back and expanded upon what made it great. This is THE definitive entry I would suggest to anyone looking to get into the the Story of Seasons/Harvest Moon franchise, or who is already a longtime fan looking to get back into it. P.S. I highly recommend getting the Pinefly DLC to support the Royal Zoological Society of Scotland in restoring the almost extinct species. It's only $1.99 and comes with a very cute outfit + gilder!

The art style is endlessly charming, and the game runs perfectly with little to no lag, glitches, or bugs to speak of. This is the best looking Story of Seasons game to date. The thoughtful animations really add a nice touch, like petals coming off when you walk through flowers, the grass swaying and shining in the wind, and the town clock displaying the actual in-game time. Though I have to mention the music, it can be very hit or miss. Some songs are grating and kind of unpleasant to listen to, while others are so lovely that I can't help but stop and listen. About the voice acting, boy am I glad they went with it and can't imagine future titles without it. It adds so much to the immersion of interacting with all the characters in Zephyr Town, and really helps flesh out their personalities, no matter how cookie cutter they may be.

Although the beginning of the game starts off pretty slow, the core gameplay loop of getting ready for the bazaar is super fun! There's lots to keep you busy, on top of the typical farming life sim gameplay we've come to expect. It's the kind of game where you tell yourself you'll play "just one more day" and before you know it hours have gone by. The bazaar itself is a blast, and it feels so satisfying to sell out and see all your hard work pay off at the end of every week. The devs added all these little quality of life improvements too, such as multiple places in town to access your storage from, bulk crafting, being able to jump, sorting & organizing your storage with a single button press, a map that shows the current location of every character, a gilder to get around town quicker, and more.

I have to mention some negatives, and for me those were mechanics and story progression. My sister was watching me play this and said it felt more like an inventory management simulator than a farming sim, and she's not wrong. 80% of this game is managing your inventory, resource gathering, and crafting, so if you don't find that enjoyable I can't recommend it. And as for the story progression, it's extremely frustrating. They locked hearts behind item requests, and they have to be of a certain quality (number of stars) to complete. I wanted to level up hearts with Arata, and he wanted a poached egg dish. No problem, I'll cook that up right now. Well that dish I just made doesn't actually count, because I used 1 star ingredients instead of 2 star. So I have to remake the dish with higher quality ingredients. And until I do, Arata will repeat THE SAME DIALOGUE OVER AND OVER AGAIN AND REMIND ME EVERY CHANCE HE GETS THAT HE'S STILL WAITING FOR THOSE POACHED EGGS. Every single time you get a request from a town member, you might as well ignore them until you have the item to complete it, because nothing you do will increase their hearts or change their dialogue until you do. It's gotten to the point where I'm going to quit the game within the next 10 hours just so I can see the relationship/marriage/having a child dialogue and cutscenes with one romanceable character and look up the rest on YouTube. The grind for me isn't worth the many more hours it'll take to see everyones' cutscenes and dialogue, especially when they made it as tedious as possible for people like me who want to prioritize the story and life sim elements of the game.

Even with those negatives being taken into account, Grand Bazaar more than blows its predecessors out of the water in virtually every way. This a huge step up for the Story of Seasons series. I can't wait to see what they have planned for the other Harvest Moon remakes in the future, and can only hope they will be as high quality as this one!

Story of Seasons: Grand Bazaar is the best incarnation of Story of Seasons yet. Ramblings will follow.

For context, I'm approaching Fall 1st of Year 1. Steam says I'm at 36 hours played but I'd easily lop off 12+ hours from being afk Dad.

This game just has tons of QoL changes that are nice, along with a wide array of goals to work towards and a very nice trickle of constant unlocks.

It never felt like I was being barraged with new mechanics/interactions/goals, but it also didn't feel painfully slow either.

In Spring especially pretty much every day you would get one new *thing*, sometimes something as simple as a tool, other times more complex things like Windmill production facilities, or a new person being introduced to the town, etc.

Every day I use up all of my stamina and then debate eating food or taking a bath to get more and go do more shit before I turn in for the day. 

It's the perfect balance of "I wanna do a bunch of shit" vs. "Do I have enough time to do this" vs. "Do I have enough stamina to do this". It's a very nice natural tension as you ramp up your production, and makes each day feel productive in it of itself.

For a game all about making money, you're constantly rewarded for re-investing in yourself, your crops, or your infrastructure.

Which then gives you another point of tension of "do I spend this money on re-investment to scale up in quality/quantity or do I buy more unlocks".

Furthermore, the game does a great job of scaling the cost of the unlocks themselves, so as you start making more money, the game *expects* you to have that money to be able to meaningfully progress, and thus constantly keeps you in a feast/famine cycle of cash on hand which feels natural.

Pretty much every single Bazaar day (Saturdays) I will set up my shop, make a boatload of money on all of the goods I have spent time crafting/farming/gathering from the prior week, and then immediately spend 90%+ of that money on a meaningful unlock via a different store.

Unlocking Mushroom Farming.
Unlocking Beekeeping.
Adding Additional Barns.
Adding Additional Crop Fields.
Unlocking more Storage.
Unlocking more QoL Features.
Unlocking Fast Travel Options.

The list is near endless and is constantly being refreshed as you progress both your farm and the Bazaar.

That about sums it up. I think this is one of the best "Harvest Moon" titles ever made in the history of the series, and if you're looking for a solid title to pick up, you really can't go wrong here.

Story of Seasons Grand Bazaar offers a charming, idyllic experience in the farming sim genre. Offering a fresh take on an older game released back in 2008. Re-imagining is a better term for this release, instead of remaster. It’s not only updated graphics that this game offers, but a completely new and unique experience, not seen in other farming sims. There’s so much that I love about this game, but to try and keep things simple, I will bulletin what I think the pro’s and con’s are. That way you can decide if this game’s right for you!

Pro’s
Progression- the progression in this game is seamlessly implemented, and very rewarding. You don’t only focus on your own farm’s growth, but the growth on the town’s bazaar as well. The game hits the perfect balance of short term, and long term goals. Offering a fun and addictive game play loop, while you work towards said goals.

Npc’s- Npc’s are cute and charming, with a bit more depth given to them as you view their cut-scenes. It’s not only the bachelor’s and bachelorette’s who’re given cut-scenes. But other villagers as well, as they go about their daily life, it’s a cute snippet of what life in Zephyr Town is really like.

Bug Free - granted each and every game has their own bugs or fixes needed. It’s unfortunately very common for games to be released unoptimized, and bugged to death. So it is very refreshing to see that after 40+ hours, I have yet to see any bugs, glitches or performance issues. I have a lower end PC so it’s reassuring to see a new game release that doesn’t set my PC on fire.

Charming details - it’s clear the game has a lot of charm and love put into it. To me it shows most in the small details as you go about your day. Running over a patch of dandelions will cause the seeds to scatter. If you have a pet cat, it will perch and sleep on  nearly any furniture inside your house. Herding your animals in and outside of their barn with your bell. All of these things are small, but when implemented together it gives a more immersive and charming experience overall. 

Character Customization - the character customization is implemented a bit better in this installment than in previous titles. Giving plenty of options to really make your farmer your own. Unlocking more clothing options as you progress helps in this area too!

Con’s 
Npc requests - once you hit a certain heart level with any npc, they will have a task or request of you. Until you complete said task, your relationship is locked out with said npc. It’s not this mechanic that I mind, but the request that they make. Anytime you speak to said npc, they will ask you about that request. Every. Single. Time. Prompting the screen to pull up said request to see if it’s been completed or not. While you can simply wave at the npc and not interact with them. I found myself instead avoiding NPCs entirely, until I could fulfill said request. It’s unnecessary for them to not only mention it, but for the game to pull up the quest too. It’s to me, the only repetitive and tedious mechanic in this game.

No house decorating - there is no house customization outside of putting flowers into a vase, and placing items on a single shelf. While the game does offer plenty outside of this, it seems a strange choice after all of the customization offered to your character, and your bazaar stall. I feel as though they could’ve easily offered some color swatches to change up the inside of the house and personalize it a bit better. However the game play is so fun and addictive that I really don’t notice how minimal the home customization is.

I would recommend Story of Seasons: Grand Bazaar. It is a fully finished game, so it is a final product and fully polished. However, that does mean that any sort of QoL updates won't likely be added to this title (such as an auto-transfer for placing all items from your inventory that are already in your storage directly in with one click — it does not have that, and it probably never will).

When it comes to Story of Seasons titles, this is probably the best since the 3DS era. Grand Bazaar is jam-packed with content and delves quite deep into the realm of cut-scenes with the Townsfolk and marriage candidates. The cut-scenes being fully voice acted was also an amazing inclusion and really gave life and character to the town. Below, I will list my CONS and PROS of the game:

PROS (The Positives)
-- Triple A quality game, fully finished, and fully polished.
-- For the first 5 or so Seasons (1 YR + 1 Season in-game), the player will have a massive amount of things to do. From selling at the Bazaar, upgrading the Bazaar, unlocking new shops and wares, upgrading tools for farming, fishing, and mining activities, and upgrading seeds, plots, storage, and barns, etc.
-- There are also a TON of cut-scenes for the game. Not only for the marriage candidates but also random events of the townies and then main story line cut-scenes as well.
-- Cut-scenes are fully voice acted, which was an amazing addition to the gameplay and story.
-- There is quite a decent amount of clothing options that become unlocked through the progression of the game. 
-- There are Animal festivals where you can get a bonus to animal products if you win, Pet contests for your Pets, Horse contest for your horse, Cooking contest for food, and Crops contest that enhance how much your crops sell for when you win.
-- Surprising PRO, but you can uproot fully mature Trees and store them until their active season. I really enjoyed this addition to the game.

CONS (The Negatives)
-- At a casual, but not intentionally slow pace, 'End Game' is only about 5 Seasons into the game (1 YR + 1 Season). As in, you can complete the Bazaar Rank easily within 5 Seasons, successfully unlocking all shops, all wares, and all upgrades. Compared to a lot of indie games of the farming and dating genre, this comes up as a shortcoming. Games like Stardew Valley, Coral Island, and the My Time series typically have much more content overall in the long-run.
-- Townsfolk + Marriage candidates and the Main Storyline are all a bit too "Disney" for me. Very happy, optimistic, sunshine, and rainbows. But, it can make up for it a bit for the fact that it DOES have some more serious themes in it such as growing up having to take care of a sibling, and parental issues. These themes are very soft, but at least add a 'relatable' note to the characters.
-- No Auto-Transfer function, and by this I mean pressing a button to automatically take any item in the inventory that exists in the storage and move it there. You gotta do it manually, each and every one.
-- Max-Upgrades for Farm Plots feels... lack-luster. Even at MAX for Farm plot upgrades (End Game), it felt like it just wasn't enough space for growing all the different crops for each season. Even at Max, I found myself having to make choices of which crops I should prioritize over others because there wasn't room for all. : (
-- 5 Star Crops: Along this same vein, I am disappointed by how the fertilizer works in this game. Even upgrading the quality of the soil does not give you a way to get 5-Star. You have to use fertilizer. Some crops output only give you 11 crops and then you have to turn 9 back into seeds (1 crop = 1 seed ratio). This just wasn't optimized in a way I am happy with.

Trio of Towns had been my favorite game in this series, and I think that this one might be an improvement. I love the mini-games, I love the characters, I even love the way you handle the animals. I don't love the lack of storage and that I always feel like I'm in a rush to get places, but I'm certain that there will be mods for that, eventually. 9/10 game

After making it to near Year 1, think I can post on this game.  This SoS game is the best version on Steam and probably the one I recommend you start with.  This is also coming from a player who has NOT played the original GB, so I can't compare how it is to the original.

Let's go through the positives:

Characters/marriage candiates/town - HUGE step up from PooT.  The events for characters are marked on the map, so it's easy to find instead of relying on a guide to find Heart events and events in previous games.  Also, the characters are lovely and they grow in their events or through the help of the MC.  All of them are different enough and most of the time, I wanted to get to know these characters from the get go.

Farming - Pretty straight forward so far, you sow seeds, fertilize them, and that's that.  What I do like is the way they handled fruit trees.  Once they're out of season, you can uproot the tree and throw it into storage for the next season.  I heard there's sprinklers, but haven't gotten that far yet.

Animals - Again, straight forward and not a chore.  You pet, you brush, get their product, and you're on your way.  What they added in is via breeding, you can get different color variations of the animal.  I got a red/brown chicken via breeding and a different variation of a silkie.  Though I did buy a pink sheep, so not sure if you can buy the color variations from the shop.  Pets are easy to take care of, although it's annoying cause all my cats want to do is sleep!

Makers - The makers this time are locked to the windmills, so you don't have half a dozen makers on the farm.  Also, no turning ore into bars or having a million different grasses and lumber.  While it is annoying to have to run to the other two in town, I think it's balanced enough with the sprite storage boxes.

Festivals - I haven't done them all, but there's a lot of them.  The crop/animal festivals return, but they are more like SoS/3oT style, which makes getting all your farmable crops to max a relative pain in the rear.  Luckily, you don't really need it too much, you make enough money as is.  I will say, bad move on the game for making the first pet derby 2 days after getting your first pet, it's impossible to win.

Bazaar - I was worried I would not enjoy this aspect of the game, but it's stressful enough that you want to make as much money as you can, and balances itself out with the trends of the month.  The only bad thing is that you save all the shopping to just Saturdays.  You CAN eventually order seeds through the week, but it's a pain because you can only order one type of seeds at a time, and not fruit trees from what I see.

Gameplay loop - It's surprising very addictive and if a farming game gives you, 'Just one more day turns into 8 hours later' type of deal, you've done things right.

Neutral aspects:

Breeding is sort of a downgrade from PooT.  One thing I loved about PooT was if an animal was breeding, they still gave you the product.  You can still pet and brush animals, but they don't give you product if they're having a kid.  Luckily, the breeding time is short, no near a month births like in FoMT!

Mining is very RNG - You can control it via the sprite, and I DID notice I got more silver in a second run powering the forging sprite to level 20.  But it's still RNG, it took a while for me to get all the orichalcum ore I needed to upgrade my hammer, and I still relied on random mail.  You CAN buy ore eventually at the Bazaar, but it's still a pain sometimes.  And ore is really valuable, it sells for a lot.  The downside is your farm is probably going to be way less profitable end game than farming ores.  The balance is that the gems/ores are very RNG dependent, so you can't really abuse it too much unless you get lucky.

Sprites - Hit and miss.  You feed them the items they want (Example, one sprite wants honey, you can give him honey or the combs to level them up) and they level up your items overall.  Some are a grind, some sprites are worth far more than others, aka the bug sprite being useless since bugs sell for so little.

Character lock - Characters can't gain any more hearts after a certain heart level, and you need to do a request to move on.  While I think this does have a good idea in concept, it can be REALLY annoying, especially if the character you're going after requires an item that is a pain to get.  Most of the time, I don't fish, and yet, I was locked out of Arata's next event because he wanted a fish.  And in other situations, you need to befriend their family member/friend in order to get closer to them, which can be a pain.

Clothes - I will say, it's definitely a step up from PooT, as the clothes have different variations of it, and there definitely seems to be more male and female clothing, but it's still a HUGE step back from the variety that we had in the 3DS games, even including New Beginning.

And some negatives:

Storage - Did we REALLY need 7 stars total, including half stars?  This game DOES give you a lot of storage space, but come on, we don't need 7 star levels, it just causes a massive amount of clutter.  If the game got rid of the half stars, I think it would've balanced itself out nicely.

Time - The passing of time goes really fast, and of course, they brought back the 'go to bed before 10, or you wake up a hour later' from PooT.  Granted, you pass out at 5 am this time, but really, the stamina penalty would've been enough.  Get rid of waking up late, or do it like in Trio, you get fatigued if you go to bed really late, and you use up more Stamina.

Dynamic seasons is gone - One thing I loved about Wonderful life is seeing the seasons change over time, the leafs changing color and falling off the trees, and snow covering the ground as you come closer to winter.  I don't know why they didn't do that here, and it's not really a negative, but I do miss it.

Rivals - Can we bring back the rival marriages PLEASE?  Why have these events if they cannot get married??  Even a freaking toggle button for it would be preferable!  It just seems really weird that your character can get married and have kids, but all your friends in town remain single.

All in all, this is a huge step up from PooT and even the other two remakes.  I can overlook some of the neutral/negative aspects of the game in favor of the positives.  Definitely a game that any SoS fan should pick up.

More than just a return to form, Story of Seasons comes back more polished and realized than it's ever been in the Grand Bazaar remake.


1) Gameplay
It feels as if they took all the best parts of the old HM/SoS and amplified them alongside the Bazaar mechanic. Trends make it so that every season has you change your tactics in money-making. The windmills and making processed goods, storage and freshness managing, at least to me, are also a big part of what makes it fun. 

The wind mechanic is also a surprise in how fun it was. I loved being able to glide across a map during extra windy days, as well as plan out all the tedious windmill-processing stuff during storms, such as jewelry and lumber.

Cons:
But my biggest gameplay nitpicks with this game lie with the unfun slowness of fishing. Fishing for me has always been a hit or miss in cozy games- I was not a fan of how involved and tedious it felt to go through Stardew's. But for this game, each button prompt felt too slow to come up, so much so that I had to mod it to be faster for me. Secondly, the animal-selling RNG at Ramon's feels very imbalanced. Sometimes you go through seasons without getting the animal you want because the same type appears so often.

It also feels as if it's lost some of the teeth of previous HM games- I want my animals to suffer a lot if I forgot to feed them for example (lol as bad as that sounds). And I also loved how cruel old HM games were about fainting, and then ending up with losing my stuff.

2) Presentation
Visually, it's stunning. It feels so polished when you see the lines of the wind on the water, a rainbow sometimes at the waterfalls, and how every season has new forms of particles (dandelions/snow/leaves) scatter about when you run through them.

The portrait arts are drawn wonderfully with this grainy, old-style about them that makes me reminiscent of old FoMT and HM Ds: Cute! Having NPC events play out with camera work and solid direction makes you much more attached to the NPCs of this game.

Plus the music is stellar- most notable for me is the nostalgic and bittersweet strings of Autumn, as well as the piano track when it's rainy during Spring and Summer. But not once have I felt that the music was ever grating. The diagetic music that evolves as your bazaar does is a great audio milestone whenever you reach each and every rank.

3) NPCs & Heart Events
I didn't get that far in the old Grand Bazaar on the DS, so I have no clue how it compares, but for the most part, the heart events in this game are wonderful. The presentation with the camera work and directing go a long way to making the heart events great to experience, alongside the amazing voice acting on both English and Japanese.

I love how some characters can go through actual conflict with one another, like Jules and Derek, and June with her familial problems. For some of the bachelors/bachelorettes, it feels as if I'm playing through a short slice of life story where I see and sometimes help them grow through their conflict.

Even the non-romanceable NPC events are mostly fantastic and fun to watch. It makes you more attached to everyone and not just the date-ables.

Cons: It feels sometimes that we're focusing too much on other people in some heart events, like Sophie's heart events sometimes feel overshadowed by her own father. It's also a shame that rival marriages are not present anymore, and I hope that won't be the case for future Story of Seasons games.

Overall:
If you were ever a fan of the previous games, getting this game hits so much of that nostalgia and so much more. There's a ton of QoLs present here that keep me glued to this game for hours on end. I feel so incredibly happy to see Story of Seasons return in such a way, where the developers also hand out these free updates periodically! It makes me feel a lot of hope for whatever new thing the Story of Seasons team can put out in the future.

Now that I have played a bit more after completing the main story and am now just about halfway through Spring of Year 2, I can confidently say this ranks among some of the best in this long-running series. A little background: I grew up playing the series with [i]Friends of Mineral Town[/i] and [i]Magical Melody[/i] being my absolute favorites, and have meandered through various other titles every now and then. Even though the remake of [i]Friends of Mineral Town[/i] was a good drop of nostalgia, it was clearly targeted at those who enjoyed the original, and it and the titles that came after didn't really move the series much. This remake, on the other hand, pushes the series forward in what I think is a fantastic direction and is exactly what the series has needed for a long time.

The gameplay loop, for lack of better words, is wonderfully addicting. Even now in Year 2, it hasn't gotten old for me as a great deal of time is still spent on preparing and optimizing for the weekly bazaar to maximize revenue even if it is somewhat less important after the end of the main story (though I have no plans on stopping and still see quite a bit to do in the post-game). Additionally, the amount of much needed quality-of-life features like festival start reminders and event icons on the world map, as simple as they are, make the game that much more enjoyable and remove a lot of the frustration when they weren't present in earlier entries. Voice acting has also made a world of difference to the enhance the overall quality of the game and injects a healthy dosage of emotion into cutscenes and standard gameplay.

With all of this, I am excited to see the same design philosophy applied to both new games and remakes of old fan favorites of the series. I can see this art style and engine working very well for a [i]Magical Melody[/i] remake and am personally hoping dearly that it is in the pipeline sooner rather than later as I would love to experience a fresh take after seeing how the developers re-imagined this game.

It constantly renews your love for playing without ever feeling overwhelming.

For me, Grand Bazaar captures that classic Harvest Moon spirit—nostalgic, charming, and endlessly rewarding—while smoothing out the rough edges that have plagued recent titles. It’s a must-play for longtime fans and a fantastic entry point for anyone new to farming sims.

This game is also a console port I think, because the PC controls leave a lot to be desired. "Enter" by default for common interactions makes no sense. I rebound it to "F" but given how it was used, I found it difficult to do some things while still moving around with WASD. I ended up using an AutoHotKey script to map the Enter/F key to my 5th mouse button, because I couldn't directly bind it for some reason.

[h1] One of the Best Framing Games I've Played [/h1]
I would say I'm a fan of games like this, having grown up with a handful of the Harvest Moon/Rune Factory games and having recently played Story of Seasons: Friends of Mineral Town. However, far and away this game is all I could want from an entry in this genre. Having just completed my first in-game year at just about 50 hours of playtime, I think a review is warranted.
[h3] The Cons [/h3]
To start, I'll get the few cons this game has out of the way. One some people might dislike is the lack of mining in the game, at least in the traditional sense. Unlike similar games, there's no dedicated mine for the player to explore and collect resources from. However, at least for me, this isn't really a problem. I never cared deeply for the mining and found it to either be shallow or annoying in other games, so it's lack of appearance here isn't one I mourn. The other notable "con" is the game's lack of a traditional shipping bin, money is made in one of two ways: selling at the titular bazaar or selling to a shopkeeper. The shopkeeper acts as a shipping bin would, giving you an item's standard value while the bazaar has a variety of factors that can increase an item's value. Which leads me into the pros of this game's system.
[h3] The Pros [/h3]
The bazaar is far and away the best addition to this game, and feels less like a gimmick and more like an evolution of the formula. Rather than shipping items for a standard rate, you're allowed to sell your goods at the bazaar. Each season has different trends, like a supply and demand, that dictate which items are currently popular. While items that aren't trending won't be negatively affected, selling items that are trending can lead to a big increase in profit. On top of giving you more ways to make money, the trends have a secondary effect of incentivising you to grow new crops or produce new items. Which leads into the second major benefit of this game's unique setting: the windmills. Being in a windy town, the player can unlock and use windmills to produce a majority of goods. Instead of buying a mayonnaise maker, you process eggs in one of your windmills to create it. This not only streamlines production, but adds a fun gameplay loop of having to produce items before the deadline of the next bazaar every Saturday. The windmills also produce faster or slower based on the current wind speed which adds an extra reason to check weather forecasts and plan your week leading up to the bazaar. The last addition that doesn't directly impact gameplay, but massively improves the game for me is the voice acting. Characters feel much more lively when they have unique voice lines and fully voiced cutscenes for different occasions. For me, it gives me more of an incentive to improve my relationships with all the townsfolk so that I can see their next social event. There's plenty more I could list about this game like character customization, the romanceable cast, or even the soundtrack but I'd be writing this review longer than I already have.

Context: 
I'm predominantly a Story of Seasons player, having played since the original "A Wonderful Life" on Gamecube. My fave HM/SoS games is Animal Parade, Friends of Mineral Town and I have a soft spot for AWL. I'm not too big on many other farming game series, but Fields of Mistria is a favorite of mine outside of SoS.

I got as far as first year winter. Haven't gotten married yet.

Gameplay:
Addicting. Hectic, but addicting. The map is not very big but time moves relatively quickly. You do need to plan your day and maybe even your weeks sometimes so you're getting what you want done. Unlike other SoS games, after farming/resources, checking the windmills, and checking in with some townspeople, it will likely be time for bed before you've combed through ALL nature-y areas for resources.

Speaking of constraints, I have a love-hate relationship with the storage in this game. It can be expanded upon, but it takes time, so you WILL have to manage it. It's not only from a quantity perspective either, as produce do eventually go bad (gradually and in steps; they usually go down in value as they get old and it takes a bit before they're straight up expired and worthless). 

It's hate because it often verged on being too annoying, but it's also love because it was also a welcome challenge for me. For comparison, in Fields of Mistria I would say storage is of no consequence (your bag storage is still limited), so having to think about storage at all in Grand Bazaar was also fun despite my frustrations.

The weekly bazaar is a refreshing, dramatic and satisfying remix of simplifying selling things via a shipping bin. Every month there are trending items that essentially sell for more and they will likely dictate what you'll focus on making. I like that there's a good incentive to make and sell things outside of just crops and animal produce. Actually selling is a fun mini game itself, as you have to balance attracting customers, checking them out before they lose interest, and your stock.

Things I like:
Combined hammer/axe
Graphics and visual style
Voiced characters
Character customization (could be improved but I like it)
Marriage candidates and two new ones
The wind and parachute mechanics are fun and useful for navigating
The game notifies you and shows you on the map when there are events to see (romance, random, etc.)
The events are fun
Windmills replace the maker machines from Pioneers of Olive Town and they're a huge improvement
Variety of pets and the fact that they herd your animals
The overall gameplay loop

Things that I don't love/could be improved/nitpicks:
The horse isn't useful for navigating town faster
Game interrupts you when your character's energy is low (happens frequently and it's distracting)
Can't switch tools/items while running
Fishing take a lot of time in the day and the mini game for it isn't fun. It's probably my least favorite type of fishing out of all farming games I've played
The spectrum for item quality is wide (whole numbers and .5 increments). This was the biggest exacerbating factor in making storage frustrating
Can't check Windmill and Animal statuses at will in your menu
I kind of wish there was more growth (literal size) and customization involved in your house
Not exploring the whole map in one day is one thing, but it feels rough to not be able to check on my plants and animals on some days, especially for animals.
Fields of Mistria spoiled me in this regard, but I wish the townspeople changed clothing throughout the different seasons
I've heard there are not many events with your spouse/partner after marriage

YMMV:
No mining
No combat

Conclusion:
This game shot up there for me in my list of favorite farming games. It's certainly up there with Animal Parade. I do think it has it beat gameplay wise, but I find that story/event wise it doesn't quite have AP beat.

As a long-time farming sim fan who has played almost every Harvest Moon and Story of Season's title, Grand Bazaar really stood out to me because it introduced something new: the bazaar system. Instead of just tossing products into a shipping bin, you get to sell your goods directly at a weekly market. It makes so much sense! Of course a farmer would bring things to their local market. The bazaar gives the game a real sense of community, with neighbors, stalls, and customers all coming together in a way that feels lively and fresh.

You’ll spend countless hours planting, harvesting, crafting, and raising animals, repeating the same cycle day after day. But to me, that’s the beauty of it. The repetition is calming, and it’s rewarding to see slow progress build over time. The weekly rhythm of preparing for the bazaar also makes the grind feel purposeful, giving your routine a clear payoff at the end of the week.

Another unique feature is the windmill system, which lets you process crops and create new goods. What makes it stand out is how it incorporates the weather — windy days make the windmills work faster and more efficiently, while calm days slow them down. It’s a small touch, but it adds strategy and makes the world feel more alive, since the environment directly affects your farm work. The pet system is also a nice addition, letting you train pets to help with tasks like herding livestock, which lightens the daily grind and gives farm life more personality. Together, these features add a new take in the genre.
