Disclaimer: This is a long one, and while I would like you to read it all, there is a TLDR at the bottom.

I am in LOVE with this game.I have been a long time Harvest Moon to Story of Seasons fan (since the new Harvest Moon games are lame), and of course I had to add Grand Bazaar to my collection. At first I wasn't sure about the Bazaar mechanic. I was honestly upset at first.... "What!? I can't just throw what I want to sell in a bin daily to get my money the next day!? Blasphemy!" But then I played, and I LOVE the bazaar mechanic and mini-game. It itches my brain so good. Also, you can still sell stuff to the in town shop Sun-Thurs if you're really short on coin, it just won't be as much as you may get at the Bazaar, but it helps in a pinch, so I really don't miss the daily bin mechanic.

On top of that, the art style is super cute, the customization is SUPER diverse, the 3D style is also very nice and not disorienting, the bachelors/bachelorettes are all fantastitc, important and main cutscenes are fully voice acted (I did notice some characters are clearer and louder/easier to hear than others which is a weird mixing issue I don't understand why was overlooked but whatevs), and the map is quite lovely and expansive but not overwhelmingly so. Despite this, I have some complaints/ideas how things could be better. 

First  I'm a bit put out that you can only get access to certain stores and such on Saturday. You get an hour in-between the morning bazaar shift and the afternoon bazaar shift when you can sell your goods, and it's honestly not enough to get everything done. The other bazaar stands close at 7pm, just like yours, so if you take up the whole time selling goods at your stand for the coin (and trust me the coin is very important), you're kind of out of luck and have to wait another whole week. I wish it was more like the main merchant shop that Miguel runs. You can buy stuff during certain times during the week, but he has more variety and special items at his Bazaar branch. I wish it was like that for ALL the services/shops. 

I also do not like how you HAVE to provide your own dye and wool for new clothes. I think it would be better if there was an option to get it for REDUCED cost if you provide the materials, but if you were to just buy it otherwise it would just be more expensive. 

The horse needs a LOT of improvement. It's walking speed is SLOWER than yours, and even more so than your running speed and there is a delay in getting it to gallup, which is kinda annoying. Controlling it and getting it to turn is also super janky and kinda hard, honestly probably the worst part of the game but not enough to ruin it.

I haven't unlocked the basement greenhouse yet, that's late game i guess, but even so, I feel like there is not enough space in your outdoor fields to plant crops AND trees. There seem to be a lot of trees in this game, as well as a ton of different crops, and if you want enough space to plant/manage crops other than trees, then you have to uproot and replant trees and that's just super sad and annoying because trees take FOREVER to grow, so you barely get anything out of them by the time they do, plus you can't plant things outside their season to get a jump on it. On top of that, they are pretty expensive to buy, so they feel like freaking money pits that your lucky to get 2-3 harvests out of a season. I'm not sure how big the greenhouse will be and that may change this aspect, but until I get it, I'm going off what i know. If it's no bigger than the fields we have, then I'm just going to be even more dissapointed/let down.

Another huge thing for me is I am CONSTANTLY running out of storage both in my bag and store room. I also do not like the "freshness" aspect much, but I get it. Storage is expensive and hard to save and plan for. The storage either needs to be MORE or it needs to be cheaper/easier to get.

My final note/complaint, is that the grind is pretty hard in the game. Once again not overwhelmingly so, but it's still a bit annoying and I wish there was a way to select an "easier" difficulty to make it a bit less stressing. I also wish you had more time before you HAD to go to sleep, and I REALLY wish everything didn't drain stamina so much. Yes, you can do things to restore stamina, but I'm only in year one and there has only been one option/chance to permanently increase your stamina, unless I'm missing something, and that is to buy a special berry from the Nature Spirits. I got it early in the second month/summer with these "happy points", or whatever they're called, and they haven't had another one since and I'm nearly to winter. I am CONSTANTLY running out of stamina and time to do everything. Yes you can make it less taxing and make your chores/actions drain your stamina less with better equipment and other small upgrades, but even with those it's really hard to get everything done that needs to get done, as well as get certain materials and the coin to get the upgrades. It's nearly impossible to buy other stuff you need, and forage, and water/fertilize, and mine, and talk to residents everyday too, so you kind of need to meticulously plan what you do everyday, but then you get behind on the other stuff. It's even hard to just get 2 of those things done in a day before you pass out and/or run out of things to restore your stamina.

However, with all that being said. It is a very great game, and I highly recommend it to any story of seasons/old harvest moon fans because despite it's few annoying things, the game is beautiful and fun, and you can literally spend hours upon hours upon hours playing and not get bored. If you love farming and dating sims, then you'll love this game.

I feel I've been a bit spoiled by indie games which gives the player the option to slow in-game time down as the in-game clock feels like it moves at warp speed when it's just the typical "1 second IRL = 1 minute in game".
Intro out of the way, into the pros and cons:

Pros:
-You start out with a house, instead of having to build it from a tent or a shack
-You already have a kitchen (although further tools do need to be purchased later on)
-Aforementioned house comes equipped with a bath which, for only 30 in-game minutes, restores a good chunk of your stamina
-The barn is connected to your house, so you can walk right into it after getting up in the morning
-Fodder for livestock spreads like wildfire, so just the seeds you're gifted are enough to satisfy your animals
-There are "happiness points" which can be spent on bazaar days in order to purchase things from the sprites; the boxes which connect to your storage are very important
-The "jump boost" to watering crops and gathering allows you to water more squares right off the bat
-Due to the windmills (which do need to be repaired at various points, but it's rather easy to get them completed), you get to upgrade your own tools; no more memorizing three or four different store hours to plan when you should pay for that upgrade
-You are gifted your first chicken, pet (cat/dog), and horse
-Dogs and cats help herd your animals in and out of the barn (dogs herd larger animals, and cats herd the chickens)
-Windmills are your production makers and your seed makers, and windy days speeds up the process.  Raising the star level of your crops by being able to easily make your own fertilizer with weeds is great
-Selling at the bazaar is easy (if not hectic once you unlock more stalls) and you can get buffs from decorations and the nature sprites
-Give the nature sprites items to increase the quality of things like foragables (flowers, grass, ect), mushrooms, honey, fish, and bugs
-There are monthly trending items for the bazaar which will increase your profits on that
-Many of the competitions can be won in your first year (not all of them, but a good amount)
-As you increase friendship with villagers, and unlock certain titles via just doing daily chores, NPCs will send you gifts in the mail ranging from needed metals to food (the latter very important to learn recipes)
-The map is small enough where it doesn't take half a day to get from your farm to the town
-You can order most seeds (and tree seeds) which you've owned previously
-You can see likes and dislikes for gifting on the NPC affection level screen, so no more needing to memorize them or write them down
-Items take time to spoil, and go through a few stages
-Colored quest markers will appear next to characters on the map, so you know who has a quest/cutscene
-Resources can spawn at least twice a day (once in the morning and once in the evening) of ever day

--

Middle of the road:
-The general store (where you buy your seeds) will sell additional seeds on bazaar days.  While somewhat fun, it also means that you have to wait until whenever it is Saturday in purchase the other two type of seasonal flower and some of the better selling crops.  Flowers aren't as much of an issue, but since some of these crops can take over an in-game week to grow it means you just lost out on a harvest.
-The mushroom logs and beehives are not on your farm.  While this means more space on your farm, it also means you have to travel up to the mountains to collect from them
-You do need to keep an eye on your quest list in case you complete one without realizing it, because there's no indication to let you know

--

Cons:
-Everything is so expensive!  This will likely be one of the first things you notice.  Initially, buying seeds will be a profit loss as you do not have access to the windmill with the seed maker ability.  Food items, as well (which are needed to learn food recipes) are extremely expensive
-Storage is extremely limited.  You can get upgrades (at expensive prices of course), but you run out super quick because almost everything you can farm/collect in the game, including foraged items like weeds and rocks, has a quality-star rating to it
-Windmills can only make up to 10 of an item at a time, and there can only be six items being produced per windmill
-The first in-game week is a nightmare of cutscenes every in-game morning.  You gradually unlock every tool you need (frustratingly, the fishing rod is last), and although you can skip some of the tutorials, the cutscene will still eat in-game time from your day
-The controls for herding your large animals are obnoxious, though thankfully you don't need to bother with it for long if you chose the dog for your first pet
-Your farm is TINY, and you need to pay thousands in order to unlock another field (and the next one is even more expensive).  This is extremely limiting, particularly since there are many good crops to grow in addition to flowers, special seeds (such as soybeans, wheat, and rice), and tea leaves
-You can't do anything with the tea leaves when you first unlock them, as you need the yellow windmill before you can start making the tins
-The only tea leaves you can use to make tins are the autumn ones (for some odd reason), which requires you to spend extra in-game time to slowly (as you can only do it in groups of 10 as I said before) use the windmill to convert your spring/summer tea leaves to autumn ones
-You need to use the sickle to collect flowers
-Ore deposits have weird loot pools.  I've struggled with getting silver (often times just getting iron), and even gold deposits sometimes still give me copper
-EVERYTHING takes stamina; that includes just picking up items like mushrooms and nuts
-You have a fridge, but you can't access it.  You need to pay (after doing a quest to set up the bazaar stall) in order to get "freshness upgrades" so that your items take longer to spoil
-There is no bug net, and how to catch bugs is one of the few things they neglected to inform you of at the start.  I had to look it up because, near the end of spring of the first year, I was puzzled as to why I didn't have a bug net.  Getting to a certain friendship level with Kevin will unlock the pop-up tutorial on how to catch bugs...but by then, you've likely already looked it up or figured it out yourself
-The sprite warp boxes only take you back to your farm; you can't use them to warp between locations  (so don't make the mistake of spending the 30k to get the one for your red windmill like I did because I thought it'd let me travel between the boxes)
-The glider is a bit wonky.  I can't even get up to the sprite house unless there's wind because of how high that platform is, and you lose stamina if you fall in the water and need to be fished out.  The other location(s?) you can get to with the glider also requires some wind to be blowing or you're out of luck on reaching the platform, and the one in the mountains has a weird invisible collider I've hit quite a few times and had to try again
-Animals can only be purchased on bazaar days, and it's RNG as to what animal the guy will have.  Now that I have the space for one, it's been at least two in-game seasons since I last saw a lamb/sheep for sale.  I haven't tried saving before the next day and reloading the save to see if it changes, but either way that's still obnoxious.

--

Overall, I'd highly recommend it.  I went in without looking anything up (initially) or watching any videos for the "do this/don't do this" suggestions, and it's a fun experience to learn what is worth focusing on as this game is slightly different from some of the other SoS games in terms of what to prioritize growing.

As someone who plays a lot of farming games, this one currently is my absolute favorite. The graphics are crisp and clean, the voice acting is well done when it shows up, the music is genuinely remarkable. The economy scales with your perceived output pretty well to keep new purchases feeling heavy instead of letting you run away with wealth, and seasonal Trends that you can play into for extra money. Honestly those alone make for a purchase I would recommend.

But I think what really sets this above and beyond any of the other farming games out there at the moment is the bazaar and the holidays. With a lot of farming games you can start to get into this blur where you set up everything on the first one or two days and the rest of the season is waiting until the next big moment, which tends to be the shuffle to next season.
- The bazaar puts a full stop at the end of every week. Even if you get into that automatic, waiting-for-time-to-pass blur, you're only in it for a week before you're now playing a minigame to actually make the money you've earned. Fun, exciting, engaging, and makes all your work setting up feel worth it.
- And the holidays only help add in variance to the middle of every week. Most farming games have holidays where you go once, hard grind the rewards the first year you can, and then it's just a waste of time. By tying actual bonuses to crop/animal value, or having multiple tiers of competition, all these holidays suddenly have so much more replay value. 

Throw on the recent addition of Bingo cards that give you missions to do to alter up your gameplay for additional reward and I can see myself playing the same save well into a few game years instead of being done after just finishing the story.

Would whole-heartedly recommend to anyone looking for a cozy farming game.

This is definitely one of the most interesting harvest moon/story of season games I've played in a long time. My favorite will always be Animal Crossing. However, this one definitely keeps you busy. You will not have ANY downtown just FYI if you want to run a successful farm, bazaar and have successful character relationships. I never went to bed before 10PM and the only reason I went to bed at 10PM was because if you go to bed later, you wake up later. So that's the max cut off time to wake up at 6AM. 
The pro's are, the town is easy to navigate and pretty short distance to and from even without your horse and no fast travel. Farming is fun, there is no actual mine, the nodes are just laying around so you get them while you're out and about which is nice in a way to not have a designated mine day. There are plenty of romance options and overall the game is just fun. You're never bored, you are WAY too busy to be bored, ever.
Which brings me to the con's. I do not like the animal set up in this game. Petting, brushing, milking, shearing each animal is very daunting every single day. I do like the fact they can't get sick in this game though. However, two full barns will take you a good 2-3 hours in the morning just to do all of that. I hate the way they did herding. You ring a bell and basically stand there for an hour (in game hour) while they all mosey their way out the door, getting stuck behind you or being too far out of reach to hear the bell in the process. Until you get a dog/cat and can spend a lot of time training them every day so they automatically do the herding. The downside of the automatic herding is, when I wake up first thing, I want to milk and shear etc...but if they're all scattered around out side it is a pain in the butt to run around and search for them all in the field adding extra time to your day.
Eventually when you make enough money and have enough yarn to make/buy clothes, you can sell most of the animals and just keep one for milk and eggs for cooking but it cuts down on the chore aspect.
Next, I hate the way cutscene progressions work. Some of them take up your whole day without you knowing in advance. So yep, if you haven't watered your crops yet but June from down town has a cutscene you catch, it could be three hours later before you can get back. Same with the bazaar cutscenes. The bazaar only runs on saturdays. But you best believe there's a story progression scene on a saturday meaning you cannot run your own bazaar and make money that week. They only let you know this on the Friday before the bazaar by the way after you've spent the whole week filling up your stall and running out of room.
There are good things about the game, its catchy, its fun, its challenging, but there are a lot of things that they definitely could do better.
Also, when you're cooking, it does NOT pull from your storage. You have to have all ingredients in your personal backpack in order to make something.
The horse also sucks. Jankey turning and no whistle to call him to your side so if you leave him somewhere oh well! lol Anyways, overall I'd recommend the game, but definitely be prepared to be a bit frustrated with how the controls and gameplay are.
Bug catching can also be quite tedious. The wind blowing in one direction also sucks. Wish it worked in both directions. And on days its slow, getting around is a lot slower.

Story of Seasons Grand Bazaar is ALL I will be playing this weekend in my spare time. I'm mildly suprised with the fact that it's actually FUN right from the start of the game (a lot of farm sim games are a bit grindy for a whole season, year, or even the whole game imo). Very impressed with some quality of life changes, and the voice acting hasn't gotten entirely annoying yet... jury is still out on the Mayor. I'm convinced there's some shady stuff going on behind the scenes regaithe Mayor - was a bit concerned I'd wake up the second day in a bathtub missing some vital organs (not really since it's a SOS game, but it's fun to speculate anyway lol). 

THE FUN: 

Jumping around, unlocking abilities to double jump, get a glider... I'm surprised at how much I enjoy it. Same with the farming! You can jump to use any tool in a 1x3 range instead of 1x1 right at the start of the game! This made it feel way less tedious to me. It looks goofy to watch but I promise you, you'll love it! 

I just love the animals in this game and I haven't even gotten to the pets! The interactions, calling with the bell, and seeing the different varieties and breeding system...I'm excited to get further in. 

Quality of Life Improvements: 

The MAP! It shows you where people are at any given time. It shows you where a cutscene will activate and gives you a tiny notification ring when it's time (instead of getting frustrated with lack of progress and going to the Internet to look it up). 

The Windmills: Way better than doing errands every day to shops in town, hoping you don't miss the window or day that they're open to buy ingredients or upgrade a tool (which took DAYS in other games). Instead, you use your windmill for most things. Tool upgrades, making byproducts, crafting for the bazaar, etc. Not having to pay for a tool upgrade and wait 1-5 days is AMAZING! 

The Jury is Out: 

Freshness: I thought I'd hate this. But so far I've had zero items loose freshness two weeks in to the game. I'm starting to wonder if they stay fresh for a whole season? I'm glad it's not making me anxious yet so hopefully it stays that way. 

Voice acting and cut scenes: There's a LOT in Spring. I'm hoping it will calm down soon after all this intro stuff, initial upgrades, and beginning heart scenes with the singles in my area. 

Bag and Storage space: Upgrade it at the FIRST BAZAAR!!! Don't wait like I did. You'll be frustrated the second week. I'm going to focus on upgrading storage every week until it's maxed... because having produce lay on the ground while you panic about storage then pick them up ONE BY ONE later is awful. Hopefully this isn't an issue for the whole game. 

The Bazaar!!! 

I was skeptical. I was worried. I was CRAZY! It's SO FUN!!! It breaks up the monotony of farming/ranching and it genuinely feels like you are at a local Farmer's Market putting produce out to sell! The mini mini game with the Sprites not so much, it's a great way to boost sales and profit but the Bazaar is fun and I look forward to it. It's also where you do most of your shopping and upgrading which removes a lot of mid week decisions for me, letting me enjoy the game more. 

If this sounds like your cup of tea and you're tired of the same old farming sim grind, buy this game! Frankly I have way more to say, but I have to end this sometime! 😂

This is the best Story of Seasons I've ever played, a great remake compared to the previous series, I've played for more than 270 hours, managed to get all the achievements and ended very satisfyingly.

[h1]Remake Differences[h1]

Marvelous Inc. has done something praise-worthy here: turning a flawed game into a good one instead of retreading an already successful title. Grand Bazaar is a tour de force in revitalizing old content. Zephyr Town is larger, with an added mountain path for basic mining. Some characters introductions have been moved to earlier in the game to better facilitate heart event progression. Windmills are unlocked sooner, making the crafting system more accessible. Crops can be turned into seeds earlier and becomes core element of maxing out a crops’ star ranking.

But let’s take a look at what sets Grand Bazaar out from the traditional Story of Seasons experience. The general farming hasn’t changed much, but what has are the crafting systems and mechanisms for making money.

Crafting is done with windmills and is on a timer system that is adjusted by the current wind speed. Drop off some eggs at the windmill, come back later, and you have mayonnaise. Each item has its own process time, and the windmill can only hold so many things in its production line at one time. Thankfully, there are three of them, each unlocking as the story progresses and each one opening new avenues for crafted goods.

The windmill system offers a greater depth to item gathering and farming that the more classic entries in the franchise never have. It feels like a bit of an apology from Marvelous Inc, for the maker system in Story of Seasons: Pioneers of Olive Town, a similar crafting mechanic that was poorly received by fans. Progression was regularly gated behing waiting for makers to produce goods, which it did so rather slowly and in limited quantities. The windmills are now much faster, having six slots of item creation, with each slot permitting stacks of ten.

On days when the wind is calm you’ll be waiting some time for the production line to clear. On windy days, your goods will develop at a steady pace. And on stormy days, it all moves along rather quickly. This adds a bit of strategy for choosing which goods to craft. On a very windy day, you might choose to focus on items that usually take longer to make, taking advantage of the accellerated crafting times. But your area of concentration will almost always be defined by current market trends, which change each month, ensuring that you vary up the kind of items you produce.

Selling is done every Saturday at the bazaar, with the shipping bin of old having been totally cast aside. You can still take some goods to Miguel, the proprietor of the local general store, if you’re short on cash, but you really want to save most stuff for bazaar day. The more sales you complete, the faster the town’s bazaar ranking grows. You’ll find that some mechanics and even story bits are gated behind bazaar progression. Fortunately, the bazaar minigame is quite fun though not overly complicated.

You have a limited number of item slots in your stall’s stock menu, meaning you’re going to want to place a higher number of expensive goods for sale, taking into account the current trending items (so sense in focusing on yogurt if cheeses is the hot item, even if the former nets large profits). Unfortunately, the gap between how fast trending items sell versus non-trending ones isn’t very large. There was rarely a time when I didn’t sell out of my stock, even when I sold mostly non-trending goods. This is a departure from the DS original which, as I understand it, often left you with product left unsold at the end of each Bazaar day. I sort of wish there was a greater incentive to focus on trending items.

Regardless, the fact that anything you put up for sale will inevitably sell makes for a rather speedy main story, as plot progression is tied to advancing your Bazaar rank. There’s something to be said for a farming game that respects your time and allows you to wrap the main quest within the first year. It’s just that I enjoyed my time with Grand Bazaar so much, I actually found myself wishing the main plot had dragged out a little longer, something I rarely find myself wishing for as a real-life father of two with a full-time job and a wife.

[h1]Writing & Characters[h1]

The plot isn’t anything revolutionary for Story of Seasons, as it follows the classic formula. You arrive to take over the abandoned farm north of Zephyr Town. As you settle in, you learn the town used to be something of a legend for the success of its bazaar, but it’s recently fallen onto hard times and has been all but forgotten. It’s your job to help turn that around. There’s some additional emotional beats regarding the mayor and the previous inhabitant of your farm that is satisfying to see the resolution to, but it’s nothing groundbreaking.

Two new marriage candidates have joined the cast, Arata and Diana. As someone who never played the original DS game, the new characters are right at home with the mainstays. I never once felt they were out of place.

The characters in general are all well-written and endearing—perhaps not as charming as the ones from the classic games (honestly, it might be my nostalgia bias showing), but still a marked improvement over entries like Pioneers of Olive Town. It’s evident Marvelous has discovered what works here.

[h1]Performance, Visuals, & Sound Design[h1]

Firstly this is the best looking Story of Seasons game ever made. Graphical impressiveness has never been a selling point of farming sims, but when the target hardware allows, it’s never a bad thing to have. Although many of the animal and character designs are rather simple, there is a level of detail in the overall world that you don’t typically see in Story of Seasons.

The soundtrack is quite enjoyable. The main themes for each season are memorable, with the winter one being my favorite (that one’s going on my Christmas playlist). There’s some variety in the tracks as well, with the music shifting upon nightfall and on rainy days (although the latter sounds a bit too much like Praise & Worship music for my tastes). The collector’s edition comes with the soundtrack on CD, and that alone made me feel better about buying a game I had no idea I’d end up loving so much.

For the first time, Story of Seasons has fully voiced cutscenes. This isn’t something I can say I ever wanted, but it’s certainly welcome. Each member of the cast is well suited for their roles, with the line deliveries for Mayor Felix (voiced by Brent Mukai), perhaps being my favorite.

[h1]Final Thoughts[h1]

I can confidently say that Grand Bazaar is the best entry in the series, making it my go-to recommendation for new-comers to the series. It seems Marvelous put a lot more passion and care into it than their previous remakes (although, I would never suggest they disrespected the source material for the others). I have to wonder what made them dedicate a larger budget to this title (no other Story of Seasons game has featured a fully voiced cast, after all). Was tbe DS original the favorite of some producer? Or did they simply see a Grand opportunity to enhance a title that previously failed to capture the fanbase? Either way, they’ve successfully enthralled the community with this attempt. Reception to Grand Bazaar has been overwhelmingly positive amongst farming sim addicts, with many—myself included—claiming they haven’t been so hooked by a game since Stardew Valley.

Full marks for the team on this entry of the Story of Seasons franchise.  While it's technically a remake of a DS game, it's actually more of a full reimagining of it for the current generation.  Art style is great and the game loop feels mostly right.  Instead of crafting product processing stations you make use of the windmills across the town to produce your goods.  And instead of a storage bin that you throw everything into for money, you actively sell your farm's goods at a weekly bazaar that is pivotal to the story progression.  Relationships with the villagers also have milestones where they have a request for you to complete to continue increasing bonds as well, and craft use of your crops to manufacture more seeds can allow you to progressively increase the quality of them in a more sustainable way with all of this leading to one of the more significant diversions to the genre's standard gameplay loop that many will find a real breath of fresh air.
With that though, these may be pain points for some as the windmill processing means you only have so many slots for goods processing which can get even more bottlenecked by some artisan goods taking days to make.  While the seedmaking allows you to eventually completely skip buying them, it means high yield ones like tea leaves and broccoli will be a go-to over most other crops.  Some of the requests from villagers that are mandatory for progression are definitely padded out heavily to greatly slow down the ability to blast through relationships and the story to a level that can feel like a significant artificial stretching of the time required to finish the game.
Those potential nitpicks aside though it's a definite high point for the Story of Seasons franchise and a worthwhile buy for fans of farming life sims even at full price.

I was obsessed with Harvest Moon as a kid. As an adult, the newer entries in the series were all getting terrible reviews, and I had no idea why people enjoyed cheap clones like Stardew Valley. However, when I saw this one pop up and it was getting a positive reception, I went out on a limb and gave it a chance. And I completely fell in love!

I LOVE the bazaar concept - instead of dumping your harvest into a box and forgetting about it, you collect everything up for a weekly market. Game progression is tied to your weekly bazaar sales, so the rest of the week is a mad dash to collect resources and craft/cook/convert them into the more valuable wares. If you're like me and the chill no-stakes vibe of other farming sims doesn't get you motivated, this is the game for you. 

This game also does a great job of taking away the tedium of many farming sims. You can hoe/water/harvest big areas at once, your dog will herd your animals for you, and you can shout "hi!" to townsfolk as you run past for your daily friendship boost. No more clicking on each individual carrot, or having to read the same dialogue box over and over again. More time to explore, mine, catch bugs, fish, etc. 

Also the game is adorable!! I don't know why previous entries in these series' have been so ugly. This game is bright and colorful, your character is adorable with many outfit options, and the animals are soooooooo cute! 

There's one big negative, and that's inventory management. Every item has a rank, and items of different ranks do not stack in the same inventory slot. E.g. if you spread fertiliser unevenly over a field of potatoes, you might end up with a bunch of 2* potatoes, 2.5* potatoes, etc... But again EVERY item has a rank, every rock, weed, ore, fish, etc, which makes inventory management an absolute nightmare! 

Oh, well, also the fishing minigame is super slow and boring. And you can't ignore it because you will keep getting quests to deliver five 3* fish ;(

- Love there's no need for a physical tool to ring in the animals back into the barn.
- Love the bug catch aspect, to improve its quality is to donate them to the appropriate sprite.

- Appreciate the autosave, but still feels under-the-rock for not letting you save anywhere incase of mistakes/crashes.
- Though I would've preferred picking up flowers instead of cutting them, which cost energy. I would understand if it was farmed-raised flowers but not wild-foraged flowers. 
- Fishing is simple, thank goodness. I'm sorry, I just don't like fishing to be a crazy challenge bobbing back and forth.

- I do like the acrobatics/parkour we're able to do, double jumping and gliding is nice. Though, still silly on why MC can't swim...are we that nomadic still?
- I'm only in Summer Y1, so there's still a lot to do, and loving the difficulty progression curving upwards as you play more.
- Lastly, I'm very sad I've experienced three crashes in the last 48 hours of playtime. All related to loading into and out of buildings, regardless of time, it was almost rng. Not sure why, but my connection is fine, my pc is up to date on windows, drivers, pc restarted, verified integrity, still not sure the cause of it. Hopefully, they release a patch to fix it.

So far, I really enjoy it and I'd give this game 8.5/10.

As a long time lover of the Harvest Moon games, following into it's change to Story of Seasons, and a player of many different farming and life sims, overall I really enjoyed this game. 

I do however think that this really comes down to what you enjoy and want in farming sims, and over the years my "wants" have started to increase based on the success and accomplishments of other games.

First, I'll focus on the pros.

[u] Pros: [/u]

[b] - Graphics: [/b]
     I think the graphic improvement from PoOT (Pioneers of Olive Town) was subtle but notable. The textures look a bit cleaner, expressions and movements look much neater, the feel is in general more polished.

[b] - Mechanics: [/b]
     I really enjoy the bazaar mechanics, it is a nice touch and a shift from the classic "shipping box" that is in nearly every farming sim. It took some getting used to, and pushed me away from hoarding supplies. The bazaar minigame and operation is fun, and easy to use. 
     They really cleaned up the "makers" problem from PoOT with the windmills, there's more of a "one stop shop" kind of feeling, which cuts down on space and keeping track of what need to be done.

[b] - Characters: [/b]
     For one, the Mayor is a riot. It was fun to get away from the usual "old cute mayor" trope (which don't get me wrong, I love). I think what npc's there are are fun, each unique, and though some fit classic tropes I think they did a good job giving them a bit more detail in their backstories. 
     I also very much liked the slight changes to relationships and gift giving. I actually didn't feel this pressure to try and rush around and gift give for everyone all the time, because the chatting as well as waving mechanics work well.
     Absolutely loved that we got a fully voiced collection of npc's this time, this was really neat, and added some added fun to watching cutscenes.

[b] - Romances, Events & Story: [/b]
     Overall, I enjoyed the romance I chose, it's cute and sweet (first one I chose was Samir). 
     The holidays and events and cutscenes throughout the year are fun, some new ones that are very fun ideas, and the dialog is much better than some past games. You actually have a sense that the characters know and talk to each other, and they have relationships within the town, beyond their individual households.
     I loved the way characters react to things you do, the first time I [spoiler] passed out and the whole town scolded me [/spoiler] I laughed my a** off. So judgy. Hilarious.


[u] Cons: [/u]

[b] - Graphics: [/b]
     Unfortunately, I think this game like many Story of Seasons and Harvest Moon games have continued to reuse assets, there is something to be said for revisiting games that have the same feeling with the nostalgia factor, but I would love to see Story of Seasons/Marvelous as a developer try and refresh their art style, not necessarily a full departure, but I miss for example the animals in of A Wonderful Life & Another Wonderful Life. They were still cartoony, but had honestly a better feeling to them compared to the characters. 
     Since these games are revisiting the same world, but are separate games, it's not the Sims 4 dlcs, it could really use a refreshed feeling.

[b] - Mechanics: [/b]
     I think the greatest lacking in mechanics is actually the crafting. Though I liked the idea of the windmills for crafting and creating products, I feel it was actually a bit to far of an over-correction from past games. As you progress in the game, it feels more and more sluggish, even with the [spoiler] stones you can install [/spoiler], there is still this drag of waiting for things to process. It needs mods to really feel more balanced the further you go in, which ultimately I would blame on scaling of time.
     Like any farming sim, I feel like we all really critique the fishing minigames lol, all in all, it's a little rough. Mostly because it's slow, it's hard to get much fishing done at once because of how long it takes just to catch one fish. 
     Improving quality of products in general feels a bit overworked. Beyond the classic fertalizing, to improve quality of fish, bugs, honey, mushrooms and foragables, when you require the player to donate the things they collect to improve the quality only feels like it works when they have an excess of that item, so for example, I feel it works okay with honey and mushrooms, foragables to a lesser extent, and feels [i] terrible [/i] with fishing and bugs because it is already a little harder to collect them. 

[b] - Characters: [/b]
     So, this has a big caveat that I understand that ultimately there is a balance to be found from number of characters and quality, as well as size of the game to be had. BUT. I think this is one of my bigger issues with the SoS games. Number of characters.

          SoS:GB has 36 total npcs, 12 marriage candidates.
          SoS:PoOT has in the base game 37 npcs, and 10 marriage candidates, plus 12 more with the expansion pass (6 marriageable)
          SoS:FoMT has 21 total, 12 of which are marriageable. 

     And then... there's games like Coral Island. [b] 50 unique villagers, and a whopping 28 romanceable [/b]. 
Honestly, this is where I think that Story of Seasons has room to grow. Now, I get that the audience is supposed to be a bit younger with Story of Seasons than games like Stardew Valley or Coral Island, I think this is probably the biggest area i wish we would see more of in the SoS world.
     Also, [spoiler] Where's our goddess???? [/spoiler]

[b] - Romances, Events & Story: [/b]
     Okay, so, kinda big issue here. WHY did we go from having a crib and separate rooms as your family expands, to "lets just make the bed bigger". Very odd choice. Don't love this. Your house does not visually change almost at all. You have a one room house, and I loved it at first, but when I realized that's all we get? it made me very sad. Not even just options to color change decor, no furniture changes, not even an extra room for the bed. Even back in the day with Harvest Moon: A wonderful life, our kiddo at least had a crib and then their own bed... c'mon guys. That was just lazy.
     My greatest other critique here is that the events are marked on your map when they become available. I waffled on this, part of me kind of likes to be able to know where I need to show up for something to happen, but, on the other hand it loses all sense of spontaneity, and instead feels like checking off a box. There's no "pleasant surprise" to experience.
     Update Added - I don't love repeated cutscenes, birthday cutscenes for your birthday vs your spouse's seems like another lazy step. The only difference is that for your spouse's birthday, they ask you if you remember what day it is. This is so far the only overtly repeated cutscene I've experienced.

[u] In Summary [/u]

All in all, I have very much enjoyed this game, this being said, I do think based on what is included currently, I don't think it is worth the current price point. I'd say wait until a sale to pick it up, add some mods for the windmills and fishing, and then have yourself some good farming fun.

I almost NEVER write reviews BUT as someone who grew up with Harvest Moon turned Story of Seasons I just HAD to write one for this game. I won't lie, Olive Town had me a little worried even though I still enjoyed it a lot. The remakes were great but I was still feeling like it just was missing SOMETHING.

Story of Seasons Grand Bazaar was always special because it had mechanics most of the other games just didn't have. It was unique and just so much fun. I am pleased to say that this "remake" is one of THEE best Story of Seasons I have played. I use "remake" lightly because while it is Grand Bazaar, it is so much MORE.

This game feels like they took note froms Fields of Mistria when it came to adding those tiny little details and love. Granted it doesn't have NEARLY as much as Mistria has added BUT this game is something I have been OBSESSED with! For me, I felt like I'd sometimes get bored or have nothing to do even when the days didn't seem very long. It felt like you just sort of cycle through the same thing and then go on the next day.

The BIGGEST thing for me in this game was the NPC's. In most farming sims it always felt...lacking? You run up to them, give a gift and be on your way. The romance character's were usually the only ones with cutscenes, but that's not the case in this game! I have been in love with learning everything about every character, romance or not! The twin's are precious and I adore them so much! Hearing them basically call their dad fat had me in stitches! The character's feel so much more alive then in previous games! I couldn't wait to see more into every character's life!

The Bazaar is obviously one of the best points of this game! To be able to sell your goods is something many players always wanted and it was done so beautifully! It's so amazing that, even with trends, you can basically sell whatever you want AND you can decorate your stall to look like that! If you want to focus on flowers you can absolutely do so! Granted I think it's best to dip your toes in everything at the beginning, but it's so much fun to be able to just sell what you want and can have a theme built around that! Instead of merely selling crops you can sell literally anything! You can focus on produce, flowers, gems, fish, foods, the sky is the limit and that's amazing to me. I don't HAVE to have farm animals or grow only crops. I can basically make money doing whatever I want!

The other NPC stalls are great too! Restricting a single upgrade may seem like a downer to most but for me it was a nice pacing tool! It made it so I didn't feel like I was just able to get every upgrade quickly and I really like that.

The ONLY thing I haven't really cared for in this game was how horses move. Maybe it's clunky at first but better with training? IDK but for me it just feels a little clunky and I'd rather run around double jumping everywhere rather then riding a horse. That's just a me thing though! Plus running feels like I can take my time and not speed run through what I need to do through a day.

If you were worried about things from Olive Town etc I PROMISE YOU WON'T REGRET THIS GAME! I cannot tell you how much I adore it. It runs amazing, it's smooth, no frame lag. PLUS there's voice acting which is probably one of THEE best things they could have ever added. Lets be real, games with lots of story/reading should just be voice acted at this point. Still not sure why Pokemon hasn't done it TBH.

All in all BUY THIS GAME!!!

[h1] Initial interest [/h1]

I saw the first trailer for this game and was initially excited that there would be a new game in the Story of Seasons series, but I could have expected that I wouldn't like it, because I don't have two of the three games in this series in my library. (Not to mention the "Rune Factory" series, which I didn't buy because it doesn't even have a basic character creator!)
Let's start with "Friends of Mineral Town": it's a remake and probably has some really cool activities and functions that could grab your attention, but those character designs! Excuse me, what's that supposed to mean!? Why didn't we get character designs from the previous game?! I don't like it so much that I'd rather play the original, so I didn't buy this game! And then there's that poor character creator.
The second game is "A Wonderful Life": another Remake with a character aging function, which worried me a little. Initially, I wanted to accept this function and buy this game, but competition appeared and of course I had neither the time nor the desire to buy this game.
"Pioneers of Olive Town": I bought it, played it and wrote a review, but this review is already outdated and requires editing. (Unless you want me to leave it)
"Grand Bazaar": another remake, I saw trailers which I liked them, I didn't think for too long and I bought it immediately.

[h1] In-game activities [/h1]

In this game you can: grow crops, breed animals, make friends and romance with the residents, collect wood and minerals, collect wild plants, take part in festivals, collect honey from bees in the forest (if you have one built), grow and collect mushrooms in the forest, produce products in windmills, catch fish and a new interesting activity that I will tell you about now.

[h1] The features that caught my attention the most [/h1]

+ Running your own stall at the bazaar - This new activity allows you to sell your goods at the bazaar. You can also decorate and improve your stall.
+ Development and attractions of the bazaar - This is also your main goal. Initially the bazaar in the game is small, but over time you will start receiving requests from merchants in another or your town. When you fulfill the merchants' requests, they will open new stands in the bazaar. Merchants not only sell their products, but can also expand your farm, teach your character new skills, and offer other interesting features that unlock as you progress through the bazaar. The bazaar is open every week, i.e. on Saturdays.
Guide - if you want to make the game easier: [spoiler] I recommend keeping 50 pieces of junk and 51 gold medals. I know it takes up space in your inventory, but the reward will be worth it. [/spoiler]
+ Mobility of our character - At the beginning, your character can jump, which will allow him to, for example, walk on the roofs of buildings. Over time, he will learn to double jump and glide, allowing him to reach hard-to-reach places where valuable raw materials are located. It's also worth noting that your character can't swim. If he falls into the water, he will be teleported to a nearby land and loses a few stamina points.
+ Many festivals - There are 4 to 7 festivals each season. (but in the first season you will only have three of them) Some of them are simply typical meetings of residents. Others are competitions in which the prize for winning is obtaining typical items, decoration for your stall, or even an increase in the value of selected crops or animal products.
+ Increasing the value of items etc. and gaining happiness points - After some time, you will encounter "Nature Spirits", each of which will require specific items from your character. For delivering these items, your character may receive happiness points, or specific items gain more value. You can also earn happiness points by performing various activities. There's a hidden "Nature Sprites" stall in the bazaar, where you can exchange happiness points for typical items, unique decorations for your stall, or even some upgrades.
+ BINGO Missions - In the mid-game you will receive BINGO missions from the "Nature Sprites". For completing BINGO missions you can get a few points of happiness, items, and for completing all BINGO missions you can receive a special reward. There are two types of BINGO missions: Repeatable which can give you a typical valuable reward, and special, where you win a unique reward. Rewards can only be collected at the "Nature Sprites" stall.
> Windmills – if you want to process raw materials, upgrade tools or do something else, you need to use the windmills scattered throughout the game world, but first you have to fulfill the request of the resident who will repair all the broken windmills one by one. Each windmill processes different products. Windmills can also be upgraded, but this requires "wonderstones", each of which serves a different purpose and can only be used once per windmill. You can also remove the "wonderstone" and replace it with another one.
> Farm - Your farm is located in the highlands. In this version of the game you can have a limited number of fields of crops and animals. Initially, you can grow a maximum of 54 plants and have 4 small and 4 large animals, but this number can be increased by asking merchants at the bazaar to upgrade your farm.
> Freshness of items – Please note that the value of some items may decrease if they are stored in a warehouse or inventory for too long. (you can see it in the item description) The warehouse can also be upgraded, so that your items stay fresh for longer.
>  The Weather - in this game is very important. In addition to rain that waters your crops, strong winds can appear that help your character glide, allowing you to reach hard-to-reach places, and also speed up resource production at windmills. During summer and winter, a hurricane may occur and destroy your crops, so you need to prepare and place a "Windscreen Kit" in the field to protect your crops from the hurricane.
> Strange outfit change function - I'm not a fan of this feature, where our character will get on the horse automatically changes its own outfit for a special outfit. This function was not available in the original version.
- There is no mine - It's a shame because these are the coolest activities in games like "Cozy Life".

[h1] To sum up [/h1]

For me, this game was the most challenging "Cozy Life" game I have ever experienced. At first I had nothing to do, but over time, when new activities appeared and I had more crops and animals on the farm, the game became more and more difficult because I had to remember everything so as not to neglect. I have to admit that the game's developers put a lot of effort into making it look quite good, but the price is quite high and it may discourage you. However, that doesn't change the fact that I don't recommend this game. I recommend waiting for a sale or looking for a game key store that offers much lower prices.
Even though it's not the best game, it's still a very good game that its creators take great care of.

Can confidently say this has surpassed HM: Animal Parade as my favorite SoS entry. Just hit the second credit roll at 76hrs and Grand Bazaar has been legen-DAIRY; it nailed the balance between charming, cozy, and addictive.

---{ Positives }---
• Gameplay loop is perfect! The bazaar introduces a unique weekly cycle, rewarding you for planning out each week instead of whole seasons
• Progression system is compelling — there are always things to improve and look forward to
• Voice acting is phenomenal and makes the world far more immersive
• Art direction and world design are beautiful, with the right balance between colorful anime and whatever they were trying in PoOT
• Windmills are my favorite iteration of makers/machines and they are actually intertwined with the world
• Ranching is fun AND lucrative. Too many games in this genre make animals a cute timesink that lack payoff
• Farming is lucrative AND fun. Overpowered like normal, but at least watering and tilling don't feel like chores
• Music is surprisingly good. I don't remember any other SoS entry where I paused just to listen to a track
• Felix is now my favorite character in the series and he isn't even romanceable. Pay his voice actor more!
• Performance is amazing on PC. Never dipped below 165FPS on max settings at 1440P with a 3070Ti/11600K/32GB RAM

---{ Negatives }---
• Time moves too fast to fully appreciate everything. Every day feels like I'm rushing around doing a thousand things
• The world is tiny. High quality, but everywhere is fully explored by the middle of the first spring (besides a small racetrack)
• Unbalanced. I'm at the end of the first year with millions of dollars from melon tea and everything unlocked besides...
• A buffalo! All I still want is a buffalo, but the animal stall at the weekly bazaar is pure RNG on what spawns

• The heart events had quality, but there weren't enough of them to actually feel invested by marriage
• I miss mines. I understand they would be difficult to implement due to how fast time moves, but rainy days without going into a mine are sad

---{ Overall }---

I didn’t expect to love Grand Bazaar as much as I do. The only Story of Seasons game I had previously played, Friends of Mineral Town, wasn’t my thing, so I was pleasantly surprised and very appreciative of Grand Bazaar grabbing me like it has.

Similar to most other farming sims: you get a farm, you plant crops, get animals, sell produce. What sets Grand Bazaar apart is the titular Grand Bazaar mechanic. Every Saturday, a few of the townies set up a marketplace, each selling their own goods or services in their adorable market stalls, from which you can buy things you can’t get on any other day of the week. You run your own stall alongside them, where you can sell your produce, crafted items or cooked meals. Decorate your stall with specific items to improve your sales, ring your bell to attract customers and make a ton of money that you can then immediately spend in other people’s shops.

Crafting happens not in a boring crafting menu, but in windmills, powered by the (sometimes too) heavy winds that Zephyr Town’s famous for. As you unlock more windmills, you unlock more recipes, and with more recipes comes more profit and more growth for your Bazaar!

If you’re a fan of farming sims, you really can’t go wrong with this one. Cute animals, tons of recipes to collect, craft and cook, a lot of quests to complete, story to unlock, relationships to build - so much to do. It’s one of those “just one more day” games you can lose yourself in. Definitely recommend it!

[h1]Foreknowledge Required[/h1]

I can't recommend this game at this time. Maybe never. There are [b]so[/b] many problems that it has and most, if not all are just unnecessary inconveniences that end up stacking up over time. It says I've only played for 12hrs and yes that's correct, [u]OVER 3 DAYS[/u]. The game just keeps pilling the rug out from under you, over and over.

From the jump! The reason I say you need Foreknowledge, is because you do. For clarification this is a remake/remaster of the HM DS version under the same title. If you didn't play that game and then you go into this one, you will be horribly unprepared. The silver lining is that a lot of the major themes in this game stay the same as the original if you [i]know[/i] to look up a guide you can generally follow the HM version and be okay.

It's like the devs gave you a soup with a fly in it. And when you ask them to take the fly out, or why it's even there at all they just tell you to eat around it. But when the dish becomes more flies than soup, can it even be called a soup anymore? That's this game in its current form. So, let's get into the Pros and Cons to give y'all a bit of an idea of what I'm talking about. 

[h3]Pros[/h3]

+ The game is pretty
+ The graphics are good and the game is actually optimized
+ It [i]does[/i] capture that SoS feel and charm


[h3]Cons (oh boy)[/h3]

- You have a storage limit. For a game series that teaches it's players to hoard their items, this is a [i]massive[/i] problem because you literally cannot hoard anything due to lack of space. You can upgrade it but it [b]costs money[/b] to do. 
- You can really only get any money or sell anything on Saturdays at the Bazaar. Doesn't sound like a problem but with the aforementioned lack of space it starts to become one. You [i]can[/i] sell items throughout the week but you get a [i]fraction[/i] of the amount.
- Any and all important/required items you can [b]only get at the Bazaar[/b] on Saturdays. If you have no foreknowledge of what you need and for what, this detail will kneecap you really fast.
- Character interactions/friendships have [i]Hard Locks[/i] that prevent you from raising your relationship with them until you do quests for them. However, some items needed you cannot get until certain things are met (ie: has to be Saturday to buy the item, a certain time of day or certain season). Meaning sometimes you just cannot continue to raise your relationship with your crush because insert silly reason here.
- There is a Freshness mechanic in this game. You [i]do not[/i] start out with anything like a refrigerator to help with this issue. Storage can help slow the degradation down but, doing so takes up a slot in your already limited space.


In summary, this game is not good and it certainly isn't worth the $40-70. At best, this is a $30-35 game and you will probably get that same amount out of it in hours played, but hate half of the time spent. This developer has a lot of better titles with similar themes, go play those. Go play Olive Town. Despite it not being optimized, it is simply better than this game in every way. Or heck, instead of playing the SoS version of Stardew, go play Stardew! I've heard they are trying to fix some of the issues in this game. Idk if that's true and Idk if it'll be enough to make it worth coming back to. As is though, it doesn't deserve to be handed out as a full-priced game when it is far from.

-The following was my first impressions from a veteran of this genre-

Probably the most glaring generic trait of this game that sinks it into the negatives is character design. You are lead by a mayor with delusions of grandeur and have townspeople that are either a walking cliche stereotype or so damn plain that their eyes aren't worth drawing more than black beads. It only gets worse from there and it feels like a novice designer making low grade cartoon characters. Regardless of growing up on this companies games, riding on nostalgia value can only go so far.

The next glaring problem is that despite being a 'farming game', you are restricted to a garden plot starting out. Consider the scale of work involved to run a ranch.. You have that infrastructure but do not have the infrastructure to run a -farm-. In reality, you are a hobbiest gardener with a ranch...

The last element to lessen my perspective of the game is the flea market. It feels like a very novice approach on the concept that Sales Blazers uses where you run a shop trying to sell whatever can go into your inventory. This game is trying to say that this town is wholly dependent on this flea market and despite the oh so credible words of the delulu mayor saying the town used to be great, has never worked with the market association required to run a market of this scale before. The goal was to tie profits to game progression and all they did was make a nonsense concept with a minigame attached to it to replace the generic sell bin. I'm not against the concept but the execution is terrible. It does however make me want to play sales blazers again though.

These three elements tank the quality of the game so hard that the low grade games of this genre look good. Song of the Prairie while having infinitely less professional programming pulls off far more appeal despite also having 60% dumpster character design.

The elements of this game that I do like are the map's build. The world very tiny but being able to jump and explore it for the first time was pleasant. While the resource gathering balance is extremely poor, pathing and town landscape was well done. This makes me think the developers should check out Palia and see how they handle their resource and map spacing.

The toolbar and inventory system is slightly annoying but very learnable which is pleasant. It doesn't take long to learn the tools even though the milker and shears are thrust into your inventory far before they will ever be used.

Character design felt nice except for the extremely gated outfits. Having every player choose between two outfits with no color palette feels like running around wearing a mascot outfit of the letter A or B. I'm the type that values character design highly and there is no reason for me to not wear this stupid unlockable cow outfit. While I still find my characters stoic but dead inside appearance in the cow mascot suit hillarious, I know the feeling will fade and become negative. This is one of the strongest player retention traits in games so neglecting it from the start is a huge red flag. I'm guessing I'll be like 10-20 hours in before gaining access to more which is going to be a dredge.

The home system looks cute at first but I have immediate concerns since I'm not able to re-arrange my furniture yet. If there is furniture grid to add and modify furniture to the home, huge red flag. There's little to no excuse to not include this as a feature in this age. Another big player retention feature as well.

I liked that I could unlock double jump, despite being painfully wealth gated, even though it did not give me access to anything I wanted it to. Felt like a scam of my first paycheck and is meant to make it easier to reach difficult jumps that you could reach without it.

The planting and watering system felt nice, no accidentally watering the dirt or throwing seeds away on misclick like many of this genre thoughtlessly include. The jumping tool use while being logically nonsense, functionally lets you spend more stamina than doing it one at a time, to do it faster which adds a level of judgement to your stamina usage for user comfort. These games unfortunately always fall when automatic irrigation comes into play which is unavoidable.

Item inventory and item storage is restricted by slots which makes me incredibly concerned given produce have individual grades and unique variants (I absolutely love this btw). Having such a small inventory space forces you to not hoard which is unpleasant but legit. Bronze grade potato, silver grade potato and gold grade potato have a freshness but also decimate 3 slots if you just leave them in your storage prompting you to sell them at risk of needing them for later progression. It's not comfortable but it still makes sense.

The chat once a day, gift once a day that this genre fetishizes allows the player to get fast reduced relationship points in passing with an AOE greeting which is nice. Song of the Prairie does something similar but nowhere near as pleasant as grand bazaar's.

I felt the handholding in the tutorial was a bit extreme and the constant popups of text walls defeats the purpose of the tutorial hand holding so much. It felt far too gated and is going to provoke those that actually need the tutorial to buttonmash through them. This is a common issue in games with a lot of articulation and little thought into user experience/user interfacing. They even include an "are you sure you want to skip?" to the dialogue which is nice but the NPC also adds lines pressuring you to view the tutorial as if you did not just tell them that you are a veteran farmer that has done this before. I regretted letting that guy talk at me his tutorial. Lol.

All in all, I am committing to this game out of nostalgia value and loyalty despite having massively negative outlook on my future experience.

Rating: 3/5 (for now) – Great potential, but major improvements needed in quality of life and core mechanics.

I’ve been playing this series for almost 25 years with my siblings, and I’ve always loved it. It’s a big part of my childhood, and I was so excited to dive into this new entry. The core charm is still there, but honestly, there are a lot of things holding it back that make it frustrating instead of fun.

First, the wholesome family-friendly feeling has slipped. The new gender option feels unnecessary and would’ve just confused my younger self. It doesn’t add anything to the gameplay and takes away from the simplicity this series has always been about.

Days go by way too fast. Please add an option to slow time down like other games do, because right now it feels impossible to get things done. The bazaar day is great, but it goes by so quickly that I barely enjoy it.

Mining is another disappointment. Instead of having a proper mine, you just run around hoping to randomly find ores and metals. That’s not fun — it feels like wasting time instead of progressing.

The quality system (0.5 star, 1 star, etc.) combined with limited storage is just bad design. If you want a quality system, fine — but then give us more storage. Having both is just punishing the player.

Some mechanics feel downright unfair. Falling into the water hurts you and makes you pass out? In the old Harvest Moon games, we could swim! Why change something that worked perfectly before?

Even basic tasks are frustrating. There’s a delay when interacting with animals, and since time moves so fast, spending a whole day talking to animals one by one feels like a chore. And why do I have to stand directly in front of them? Just let me interact from the side or behind.

Finally, the horse training system seems broken. Mine has been stuck at 1.5 fire even though I keep training and get notifications that it’s increasing. The record doesn’t update, which makes it feel pointless.

I still like the game, but all these quality-of-life issues are piling up. It makes me sad because I used to play Harvest Moon for years, and here I feel like I’ll stop after just a month. Please fix these problems — because underneath all of this, the heart of the game is still something I love.

This is a mixed review but I am marking it as negative because most of the negative reviews will only talk about the pronouns. All I will say on that subject is that the last two entries to the series had pronouns too but it was even worse because there was no body types. Just one body type so you had to play as a flat chested female and I didn't like that. This is an improvement in comparison. 

I have played around 20 hours so far and don't feel the urge to keep playing. I feel like I have seen all the game has to offer and not sure if I really like it or not. Since I didn't get much play time out of it I feel it's not worth the price I paid. Which was $75 AUD. This game has a higher price than their previous entries. I didn't enjoy those games so I wasn't planning on buying this but I played their latest Rune Factory game, Guardians of Azuma, and really loved that game. This one looked good so I thought I would give it a chance. I never played the original so this is all new to me and I won't make comparisons to the original. 

What I like:

- You can have a female body this time around.

- The characters are cute and the town is cozy.

- The voice acting is a nice touch and makes the characters feel alive. There is only full voice acting for cutscenes though.

- Jumping on the booster barrels and double jumping around town can be fun.

- I like jumping to water and harvest crops.

- Running the Bazaar can be fun (but it's short lived.)

- Graphics are very nice on PC.


What I don't like:

- The quality star system...everything has a quality system and it starts at 0.5 stars and stops at 5 stars. Characters will request stuff from you and ask for a certain quality. It's dumb, say I have a 1 star fish but they want a 3 star one...I can't just give them the 1 star! I have to grind up the quality of the fish I catch by catching a bunch of fish and then giving them to a sprite who will then increase the quality of future fish I catch...that isn't fun. It's a pain. 

- I don't like giving my stuff to the sprites to increase quality. It feels like a waste of the resources I spend time collecting. I could be selling these things at the Bazaar instead.

- I don't like being punished for falling into the water by accident. And it will happen a lot when you're trying to jump across a river or when you're using the glider and fall into the water. Every time you get punished by having some of your stamina deplete and of course you may faint on the spot and wake up the next day if it's low enough...(this makes me mad.)

- The game doesn't give you a tutorial for bug catching until you catch one...I didn't catch one for a long time because I thought someone was going to give me a bug net. You don't use a bug net, you use your bare hands to catch them. (I remember older Harvest Moon games being like this but I forgot. I guess the game just expects people to know this?)

- Using fish bait on your fishing rod is also confusing. You can't equip it in your bag. You need to equip it by holding it when it's on your toolbar. Odd.

- The Bazaar itself is fun but it's hard to use the tables on the sides and you need to be fast. If you're not fast enough customers will walk away and you will lose sales.

- I don't like needing to use the bell to get peoples attention at the Bazaar. I feel they should look at our stall on their own, maybe use the bell for some people...but it can be overwhelming to try and get people to look at your stall while also putting things on the table and checking out customers.

- You spend all week preparing for the Bazaar for it to go by so fast...it's only a few minutes at a time, there are two shift periods (which gives you a little time to shop at the other stalls in between and to restock). The pacing feels bad. It also feels like work after the novelty wares off. Everyone expects you to go to the Bazaar every Saturday and you're meant to spend the week preparing for it so you don't have much freedom to do other things. Everything you craft, everything you do is for the Bazaar (besides building relationships I guess?).

- I don't like the buzzer noise the game makes when your stamina is running low. It makes me feel like I'm doing something wrong. I don't know why they made the sound so stressful in this type of game.

- You need to water your crops twice a day. You can only do it once if you really want to but they will grow slower...I just want to water once and be done with it and not lose out on faster grow times.

- Each tool you upgrade has a second "+" upgrade. So say you upgrade your hoe to a copper hoe, the next upgrade is "copper hoe +"..which I guess is slightly better? It's just unnecessary. You will need the copper hoe + to upgrade to the next level being the silver hoe...then the silver hoe +. What a drag.

- Each windmill can only craft/process six things at a time. You will be using the Red windmill a lot early game because you won't be able to craft any of the recipes for the Blue windmill at first. Yes, each windmill makes different things.

- Travelling to each windmill is a pain (there are three of them). We need a teleport to get there. I don't know if that's an option later...I've only played 20 hours.

- Having to pet/brush/pick up each animal is a nightmare once you have a lot of them. You need to do that each day to increase your relationship and their production quality.

- Ores change location when the seasons changes...so you will have to find where certain ones spawn all over again.

- Fruit trees take up too much space in the small farming areas. We should have a special tree area.


Bugs:

- I encountered a weird bug while I was playing with my PS5 controller. The game would randomly stutter every 30 minutes or so and then my controller would be disconnected. It was charged so that wasn't the problem. Something weird was happening with the game.

- Some typos in dialogue.

Overall I am disapointed this game didn't make me fall in love with it. But it's not a terrible game and I'm sure some people will enjoy it.
